picks.headline: Opening Odds for Virginia Tech-SMU Place Hokies As The Underdogs
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech football will enter its Week 10 matchup against SMU in a relatively unfamiliar position this season: as the underdog. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Hokies enter as 6.5-point underdogs. Virginia Tech is 1-0 in its only game as an underdog, which was against Clemson on Oct. 24 in Clemson, S.C. The Hokies became bowl-eligible with their 20-16 win over the Tigers; quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's fourth-and-1 throw to tight end Luke Reynolds gave Virginia Tech a lead with 1:44 left it never relinquished. Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) opened its season with four straight wins for the first time since 2017, defeating VMI (73-3), Old Dominion (44-21), Maryland (35-26) , and Boston College ( 21-14) before its first loss came on Oct. 2 against Pitt. The Hokies got out to an early 14-0 lead over the Panthers but conceded a 35-10 run that left it in an 11-point hole. Virginia Tech totaled nine points off a Davion "FatRat" Brown touchdown catch and a Noah Chambers safety, but fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal as time expired was ruled no good, resulting in a 35-33 loss to Pitt. Virginia Tech lost to Cal in Berkeley, Calif., the next week, scoring a season-low 20 points as its defense was sliced by Golden Bears backup Jackson Brousseau for 321 yards. That 321-yard total was the second-highest of Brousseau's career. The Hokies yielded a 14-play, 79-yard drive that elapsed just over seven minutes to Cal in the fourth quarter, giving the Golden Bears a 19-14 lead. And though Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown of its own with 1:15 left, Cal marched down the field in six plays and 75 yards — 30 of which arrived via penalty (roughing the passer, defensive pass interference). Virginia Tech drove down the field, setting up one final opportunity from Cal’s 7-yard line with three seconds remaining. However, Grunkemeyer’s pass intended for Reynolds in the back of the end zone fell incomplete. Virginia Tech's Week 10 game against SMU is set for Friday, Nov. 6, at 7 p.m. ET, with coverage for the contest being carried on ESPN. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Time and date: Friday, November 6 at 7:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-6) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 2-1 Last meeting: SMU 28, Virginia Tech 25 — September 21, 1974 Current streak: SMU, 2 (1973-74) Setting the scene While No. 1 Miami (FL) and No. 14 Wake Forest are the only ACC teams that reside in the AP Top 25, the conference title race is far from finished. There are five two-loss teams lurking right behind, and two of them clash Friday night in Dallas. It’s the first meeting between SMU and Virginia Tech as ACC opponents, however, it’s a familiar head coaching matchup: Rhett Lashlee and James Franklin stood on opposite sidelines as recently as 2024 in the College Football Playoff. There’s plenty on the line for the bowl eligible opponents. A win would do wonders for remaining in the ACC race, especially for SMU, which can still capture a tiebreaker against Wake Forest. But a third conference loss is essentially an elimination in a 17-team league. Virginia Tech Hokies outlook Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) can make another statement on the road after its bye week. The Hokies haven’t rattled off seven wins in a regular season since 2019, but that streak could end Friday in year one of the James Franklin era. Virginia Tech is fresh off its biggest win under Franklin, taking down Clemson 20-16 in Death Valley on Oct. 24. Close games have been commonplace for the Hokies this season. Each of their last six contests were decided by 10 points or fewer. Three featured lead changes in the final five minutes, while another ended on a missed field goal attempt that would have resulted in a lead change. The restoration of Virginia Tech football can be attributed to the passing game. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer followed Franklin from Penn State and has drastically improved in his junior campaign. Grunkemeyer has connected on an efficient 71.4 percent of attempts — seventh nationally among quarterbacks with 100 attempts — and has delivered 17 touchdowns against two interceptions. Grunkemeyer has eclipsed 300 yards three times and finished seven of his eight starts without throwing a pick. Two receivers have carried a bulk of the load. Wide receiver Que’Sean Brown ranks atop the team with 51 receptions and 685 receiving yards, and he’s secured at least five receptions in all eight games. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also been a matchup nightmare for defenses. Reynolds’ 50 receptions rank first and his 491 receiving yards ranks third among all FBS tight ends. While a bulk of his production occurred in September, his outing against Clemson was a productive one, snagging two touchdowns on seven receptions. The Hokies aren’t as adept in the run game, where they check in at 111th in the FBS with 3.7 yards per carry. They don’t incorporate much quarterbaack mobility and primarily rely on the duo of Jeffrey Overton Jr. and Marcellous Hawkins Jr. Overton, a common weapon in the receiving game, showed the extent of his powers in a 209-yard rushing explosion against Boston College. Hawkins has been a steady secondary back, and he’s tied for the team lead with five rushing touchdowns. Virginia Tech only surrendered more than 26 points once this season, and that was a Friday night matchup against Pittsburgh. The Hokies’ defense has been a positive for the team, tied for 35th in points allowed and ranked 27th in yards allowed per game. Their strength involves limiting the run, where they give up just 93.4 yards per game on a 3.0 average. Sacks heavily factor into that total, and Virginia Tech is the best in the ACC and the sixth-best in the nation at getting to the quarterback, producing 3.4 sacks per game. It’s a defensive end led effort. Aycen Stevens ranks first in the conference with 8.0 sacks, while his fellow defensive ends Cortez Harris and Mylachi Williams have 5.0 and 4.5, respectively. The Hokies haven’t been as strong on the back end, but they prevent explosive plays well. No team has recorded a 50-yard completion on this defense all season. But what Virginia Tech needs to improve upon is its turnover output. The Hokies forced just five takeaways through eight games, causing the team to enter Friday with a minus-4 in the turnover battle this season. SMU Mustangs outlook SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) dropped from the rankings after a heartbreaking 30-27 loss at Syracuse last weekend. It was only the Mustangs’ fourth conference defeat since joining the ACC, and the third in which they held a lead in the final minute. However, SMU has never lost back-to-back ACC games and owns an 11-0 record in ACC play at home, giving Rhett Lashlee’s team the perfect opportunity to bounce back and remain in the conference title race. Slow starts have been the Mustangs’ kryptonite. In their last five ACC games, they haven’t scored more than 13 points in a half or entered the break with a lead larger than three. However, they’ve won each of their last five second halves, finishing a plus-68 over that span. SMU’s offense is led by Kevin Jennings, who is one of seven passers averaging over 300 yards per game. This season has been a masterclass in efficiency for the senior, who is completing passes at a 73.7 percent clip — the third-highest rate in the country among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. Jennings has also thrown 152 consecutive passes without an interception, with his last misfire coming in the first quarter of a Sept. 26 matchup against Missouri State. The Mustangs’ receiver room is as deep as they come, with five different players over the 200-yard threshold. Yamir Knight is the leader with 44 receptions for 523 yards, while Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale can also pose as explosive threats for an offense that ranks fifth nationally in 50+ yard receptions. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrstrom are also incorporated into the passing game, and they tie for the team lead with four receptions apiece. Unlike SMU’s first ACC defeat at Louisville, last Saturday’s loss to Syracuse was largely determined in the trenches. The Mustangs uncharacteristically allowed six sacks, accounting for 43 percent of their season total. Additionally, they struggled to create space for the running backs, which never broke off an explosive gain. Kendrick Raphael has posted three 100-yard games already in ACC play, and he can also do damage out of the backfield as a receiving option. SMU’s defense didn’t necessarily have a bad outing at Syracuse, limiting the Orange to 5.9 yards per passing attempt and 3.7 yards per rush. But the Mustangs surrendered conversions on all four of Syracuse’s fourth down attempts, allowing the Orange to sustain otherwise lost drives. A veteran defensive line full of super seniors is the strength of the unit. SMU ranks 15th nationally with 2.9 sacks per game, and eighth-year senior Marques White leads the way with 5.5 sacks, while the rest of the sacks are quite evenly distributed. The pressure goes hand-in-hand with a strong passing defense, and SMU ranks 28th nationally in fewest passing yards allowed at 182 per game. That is the most improved element of the Mustangs from last year, but losing starting strong safety Tyren Polley for the year could make things difficult down the road. Sael Reyes stepped up last game with 10 tackles in his second start of the season, while Jimmy Wyrick recorded eight from the other safety spot. Lastly, turnovers have been a significant determinant in SMU results this season. The Mustangs lost the turnover battle 5-0 in their two losses, and they’re the only bowl eligible team at a minus-5 or worse this season. These 6-2 teams are structured somewhat similarly: strong passing attacks with tight end utilization, dominant defensive fronts that repeatedly get to the quarterback, and solid defenses hampered by poor turnover margins. Short weeks oftentimes favor the home team, and SMU remains perfect against ACC opponents at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Given SMU’s discrepancy between first and second half performance, Virginia Tech may enter halftime with the lead, but the Mustangs ultimately rally behind Kevin Jennings in the fourth quarter to secure a one-score win on The Hilltop. Syracuse rallies past No. 19 SMU, 30-27 Syracuse rallied with a late touchdown drive and recovered a fumble on SMU's final possession to beat the No. 19 Mustangs 30-27 Saturday at the JMA Wireless Dome. Steve Angeli found Noah Meyers for a 2-yard, go-ahead touchdown with 17 seconds remaining, and Tripp Woody added the extra point to finish an 11-play, 68-yard drive that took 3:19, according to Syracuse's official statistics and the ACC Digital Network highlight . The Orange improved to 4-4 overall and 2-4 in the ACC, while SMU fell to 6-2 and 4-2 in conference play. picks.blurb: BYU vs Utah Prediction: Odds, expert picks, team and player news, betting trends, and stats - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Vaughn Dalzell · NBC Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 3:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Big 12 is heating up, and the conference's biggest game of the year takes place this Saturday at Rice-Eccles Stadium between #9 BYU (7-1) and #3 Utah (8-0). It's the Holy War! Both teams sit atop the Big 12, and the winner of this game is likely in the Big 12 Championship, whereas the loser can't afford another loss to make the conference title game. Utah is enjoying its highest ranking in program history, and depending on what happens this weekend, the Utes could end up No. 1. Devon Dampier has led an electric offense averaging 38.9 points per game (11th) in Kyle Whittingham 's first season at the helm, but the defense has been incredible! The Utes have been a tank from the start. Utah averages 10.3 first-quarter points per game (T-4th) and allows 0.9 (1st) defensively. Utah has gassed up opponents early and carried a lead late; that's been their M.O. Utah is on the nation's longest winning streak, 14 games, after thrashing Cincinnati 49-25. The last loss came against BYU 24-21 last season. Utah can get revenge and, in the same breath, claim control of their destiny and the Big 12. If BYU loses to Utah, the Cougars' college football hopes will rely on winning the Big 12 Championship. With a loss to UCF, BYU put their season on thin ice as Utah, BYU, and Texas Tech battle for the top two spots. BYU had a strong first half against Arizona State last week, leading 17-3 at the break, but was outscored 17-10 in the second half. BYU could get a boost this week with star running back and 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year LJ Martin returning. Martin has missed the last four games and put a lot of the offensive pressure on Bear Bachmeier . While reports say Martin won't be 100 percent if he plays, at least he could be a decoy that sets up Bachmeier in RPO or the downfield pass game. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch BYU vs Utah Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Time: 12:00 PM Eastern Site: Rice-Eccles Stadium City: Salt Lake City, UT TV/Streaming: ESPN | ABC Game Odds for Utah vs BYU The latest odds as of Thursday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Utah Utes (-198), BYU Cougars (+164) Spread: Utah -5.5 (-105) Total: 48.5 points Head Coach: Kyle Whittingham 2026 Record: 8-0 (5-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 38.9 (11th) Defensive Points Per Game: 15.8 (15th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 83rd 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 34th The Utah Utes Offense: After scoring a season-low 21 points in the win over Houston, Utah scored a season-best against P4 programs, putting up 49 points against Cincinnati. The Utes had 27 first downs, converted 7-of-11 third downs, posted 534 yards of offense, and averaged 6.4 yards per carry. Utah scored a ridiculous 42 points in the first half and led 42-6 at the half. The Utes scored on all four of their offensive drives in the first half, and the defense recorded a pick-six and fumble return for a touchdown. The Utes didn't score on the first four drives of the second half, but it didn't make much of a difference; the damage was already done to the Bearcats. Utah enters hot and ready for a shootout at 10 AM their time! Utah Player to Watch on Offense: QB Devon Dampier For the third time in the last four games, Devon Dampier threw three touchdown passes and 200-plus yards in seven straight. Dampier's been on fire, and even when he's not slinging touchdowns, he's running for them. Dampier had 150 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Houston, then turned around and threw for three scores on Cincinnati. In the last four games, Dampier has 12 total touchdowns to one interception and averaged 309.5 total yards in that span, with Utah scoring 34.5 points per game. The Utes have been a tank, and if they win this game, Dampier can jump into the top five odds for the Heisman. The Utah Utes Defense: Utah's defense has been one of my favorite units to watch this season. They fly around and lay the boom on opponents from the opening drive. Utah allowed over 200 yards in the first half, but Cincinnati couldn't convert in the red zone, nor on the money downs. Cincinnati went 3-of-13 on third and fourth downs and only managed a 24:30 time of possession. It was a dominant performance from Utah, and in the first quarter, they've been the best team all season. Utah's defense has allowed six total first-quarter points all season and a 0.9 first-quarter points-per-game average, which leads the country. Getting off to a quick start seems impossible for opponents this season; let's see what BYU can do. Utah Player to Watch on Defense: DB Jackson Bennee In Utah's biggest game of the season, Jackson Bennee posted a season-high eight tackles, had a sack, forced and recovered a fumble against Houston, then recorded four tackles against Cincinnati the following week. No. 7 BYU visits No. 3 Utah on Saturday, November 7, in the first Holy War where both teams are ranked in the top 10. The 10 a.m. local kickoff at Rice-Eccles Stadium adds another wrinkle. Utah is 8–0 and sits atop the Big 12 at 5–0. BYU is 7–1 and shares second place with Texas Tech, but its loss to UCF leaves little room for error. Utah opened as roughly a 5.5-point favorite with a total of 48.5. These predictions go against the safe script, a ground-game surprise, a Utah quarterback performance and a late BYU rally that falls short. Let's take a look at the bold predictions for this marquee matchup. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) LJ Martin plays, but Bear Bachmeier is the star Rob Gray-Imagn Images LJ Martin will return and play a limited role, yet Bachmeier will be the one who carries BYU's offense. Martin has missed four games with a leg injury and has not played since the October 3 win over TCU. He is still BYU's leading rusher at 344 yards and 7.8 yards per carry, so the Cougars badly need him. But offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick said Martin is "not all the way back yet," which suggests a managed workload. The prediction is Bachmeier throws for 275 yards and rushes for two touchdowns, outproducing Martin in every category. Bachmeier has already accounted for most of BYU's rushing output without Martin, with 336 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns on 80 carries. He also has 1,750 passing yards and 12 touchdowns. Utah's secondary is among the best in the country, so BYU may need Martin's presence as a decoy more than as a workhorse. That could open play-action and RPO looks for Bachmeier. Devon Dampier and Wayshawn Parker combine for 300 total yards Utah's offense will hinge on its quarterback and running back, and together they will account for 300 total yards and four touchdowns. Dampier has been outstanding, with 12 total touchdowns against one interception over his last four games. He has completed 69.6 percent of his passes for 1,876 yards and 18 touchdowns this season. Parker is the other half. He has 726 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, and Utah's ground game ranks eighth nationally at 226.9 yards per game. BYU's rush defense is strong in raw yardage, ranking 20th at 100 yards per game, but Covers notes it ranks only 74th in rush success rate. That gap suggests Utah can win with misdirection and efficiency instead of pure power. The Utes also rank third nationally in third-down efficiency at 54.1 percent, which helps them sustain drives against an aggressive linebacker group. Utah will lose right tackle Kelvin Obot for the season, but the line has still been one of the best in the country. I expect the Utes to handle his absence. Utah wins 31–27 and snaps BYU's three-game streak The final prediction is a four-point Utah win that comes down to the last possession. BYU has won three straight in the series, while Utah had won nine in a row before that. Utah has still won 14 straight overall, the longest active streak in the FBS. Utah's offense should control the game early, but BYU will keep it close by converting in the red zone. A late Cougars touchdown will make it a one-possession game before the Utes' defense finishes with a stop. The projected 58 total points would clear the 48.5-point line comfortably. The point spread would also come down to a single score, giving BYU a cover as a 5.5-point underdog. The result would leave Utah in prime position for a Big 12 title game berth and a playoff bid. BYU would stay alive in the conference race, but it would have almost no margin left. Here is how I'm wagering college football Week 10. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . No. 9 BYU @ No. 3 Utah This Holy War might be the holiest of them all: Utah hosting bitter rival BYU, with the winner in the driver's seat for a Playoff spot. It’s the first time both teams have been ranked in the top 10 for this matchup, and I can’t wait to start the day with this one. I think BYU might win outright. It has been tested with its win over Notre Dame just a few weeks ago. Yes, it lost to UCF the following week in a typical trap game — big home win followed by a road conference game. Otherwise, the Cougars have handled business, even though the scores don’t seem that impressive. BYU is built on defense. It is 13th in yards per play and it limits explosives. It does not rush the passer all that well, but against Utah’s rushing attack, that might not be needed. BYU’s defense already faced a high-powered offense in the Irish and limited it to a negative EPA rushing day. Utah’s offensive production slowly ticked down when conference play started, but it did bounce back last week against a poor Cincinnati defense. Utah has played one defense in the same realm as BYU and that was Houston. Utah struggled to score, only putting up 21 points with seven of those happening super late after forcing a Houston turnover. Will the BYU offense find a groove against Utah? (Getty Images) It’s fair to also believe BYU’s offense might struggle in this game. However, it appears the Cougars are getting stud running back LJ Martin back, and they are much better when Martin is on the field. He’s averaging almost eight yards a carry with 20% of his rushes going for 10+ yards. Utah’s defense is the typical physical front against the run, but BYU is the best offense the Utes have faced all season. Utah’s pass rush concerns me. It is 80th in pressure rate and unless it blitzes, it isn't able to get to the quarterback. Seems less than ideal against BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier. I see these teams as even. They are both defensively based with an offense that wants to run the ball. That’s too many points in a game like this. I’ll take BYU to cover. Schwartz's Pick: BYU -4.5 No. 5 Alabama @ No. 14 LSU In the newly-released CFP rankings, Alabama is fifth and is an underdog at LSU by almost a touchdown. I do lean towards LSU at -6, but that number feels big. Instead, I’m going to fade Alabama’s offense in this game. Alabama is facing its fourth straight difficult defense, and in the first three games, we’ve seen the offensive efficiency drop. Quarterback Keelon Russell is nearing the end of his first season as a starting quarterback, and he’s been mostly excellent for his age. However, he has struggled the last three weeks outside the end of the Texas A&M game. Against Georgia, Tennessee and A&M, he completed only 60% of passes with just four passing touchdowns and three interceptions. Alabama’s beat-up offensive line has allowed 11 sacks in the three previous games. Now, the Tide play an LSU defense that’s first in sacks per pressure and 11th in pressure rate. The Bama offensive line and Russell were noticeably affected by the environment in Tennessee, and now they are at LSU. I feel most comfortable with Alabama not scoring much in this game. Klatt's Week 10 Picks Updated Nov. 5, 2026 11:36 a.m. ET share facebook x reddit link The long-awaited, top-25-filled Week 10 of the college football season is finally here. Everything from College Football Playoff implications to potential conference championship matchups are in play this Saturday. Starting at 12 p.m. ET, No. 9 BYU heads to No. 3 Utah for the annual Holy War rivalry matchup, with instant CFP and Big 12 title impact. The day ends with No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre Dame in a rematch of the game that arguably kept the Fighting Irish out of last year's CFP. Especially after Tuesday's first CFP rankings of the season — which FOX Sports' Joel Klatt raised concerns about — this weekend's slate will make a heavy impact on the postseason playoff picture. Here at Klatt's Week 10 picks and previews, from the latest episode of "The Joel Klatt Show": No. 1 Miami (Fla.) vs. No. 11 Notre Dame (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Spread: Notre Dame -5.5 Moneyline: Notre Dame -238, Miami +195 Klatt's thoughts: " Notre Dame, you got to win … The committee really put Notre Dame behind the eight ball. They're backed into a corner. So, don't we all expect to get Notre Dame's best? I mean, we have to … Now, Miami has taken care of business. Notre Dame did not. They got beat by BYU. Yes, there was a second left. They didn't get that snap, and so here they are with their backs against the wall. "Let's take a look at this game from just like: what's the strongest thing? What's the weakest thing that any of these teams do? Well, if you're looking at the weakest thing, I always look at that, because in a matchup game typically the weakest link of the teams is what's going to end up getting you beat, and the weakest thing that anybody does in this game is Miami's defense, and we've seen that over the last, what, three weeks and three games. Two of the last three games, they've given up 35 points to Florida State and UNC. So it's not a great defense. It is not nearly the defensive front that they had a year ago. Their secondary is not great. "So they've got to find a way to limit CJ Carr, who I think is one of the better quarterbacks that we have in the country. What's the strongest part of this game? It's Miami's offense. It's interesting. They've got the strongest part. They've got the weakest part. Their ceiling with their offense is outstanding. I think it's the best thing anybody does in college football. Darian Mensah film is fantastic. I love watching it. "I'm going to go to Notre Dame. I think that they have to win, and they will win because, again, the committee is doing Miami no favors here … Notre Dame 30-27. Miami, I'll take the 5.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Notre Dame Klatt's pick against the spread: Miami +5.5 No. 9 BYU vs. No. 3 Utah (Photo by Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Spread: Utah -4.5 Moneyline: Utah -198, BYU +164 Klatt's thoughts: "BYU at Utah. Holy War. 4.5 is the spread here. Utah is favored. Utah has lost three straight in this series, including a home game. BYU has not looked great since the Notre Dame game. I think we would all agree with that. Utah has been a team that has been very impressive, which is largely why they're ranked No. 3 in the country right now. Because even though they've played something north of a wet paper bag, the committee decided that they were the third-ranked team in the country. That was a shot. It wasn't meant to be a shot. Because I love Utah. You know I love you, Utah. Death, taxes, Utah football. They roared back against Houston after being down 10-0 at around halftime. They destroyed Cincinnati. They're a difficult team to beat on the road when they're in their home stadium. Devon Dampier and Wayshawn Parker are dynamic. The one concern I would have for Devon Dampier is the turnovers. "You can't do that in this game, not in this game. And, in particular, with an aggressive BYU defense … They're going to have to run the football, play quality defense, and use the energy of that stadium to their benefit. LJ Martin for BYU could be back. I don't know how effective he will be, but they need that because they have not been able to run the football very well over the last couple of weeks. Speaking of BYU, both have good defenses. Although, gosh, you know I love Kalani Sitake. I think Kalani Sitake is fantastic, but his defense the last couple of weeks hasn't been like BYU standard. I personally believe this Utah team has something to prove. Almost like their coach retired and then took another job somewhere else. It's like it resembles that. I don't know if that was the case or not, but that's what it looks like. And Morgan Scalley has been there for a long time, and he understands the culture of Utah. And I think this team is playing with an edge. " Utah 27, BYU 20. Utah covers the 4.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Utah Klatt's pick against the spread: Utah -4.5 No. 2 Georgia vs. No. 10 Ole Miss (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Spread: Georgia -3.5 Moneyline: Georgia -175, Ole Miss +145 Klatt's thoughts: "Georgia at Ole Miss. This one could be a great game. I really think it could be. Georgia is favored by 3.5. Rematch to that quarterfinal from a year ago. Ole Miss won that one. Trinidad Chambliss was outstanding in that ball game, and I'm sure Kirby Smart has had nightmares about Trinidad Chambliss ever since then. And now he's got to go to Oxford, and he's got to play Trinidad Chambliss where Trinidad Chambliss has never lost a start. Ole Miss is not going to have Kewan Lacy, he's likely out in this game. Trinidad Chambliss is a guy that I love. You guys, I know I've loved him ever since the beginning of the year, and now he gets to face Kirby Smart. And this team is the best road team that we have in the country over the last several years. Why? Because they're consistent. Why? Because they run the football. Because they play good defense. These are the things that travel. These are the things that allow you to have success on the road. I do think it's going to be a close game. I don't think Georgia is going to be able to separate in this game, but they're too consistent. They're too consistent. "If Georgia can hold Ole Miss to field goals, I think that's where the game is won or lost. If it's high scoring, I favor Ole Miss because Trinidad runs wild. If it's lower scoring and in the 20s, then I favor Georgia because it's a slug fest, and you're kicking field goals, and it's third down and it's situations. What do I think it's going to be? More of a slug fest. "I'm going to take Georgia 28-24 . They cover the 3.5 on the road." Klatt's straight-up pick: Georgia Klatt's pick against the spread: Georgia -3.5 No. 23 Oregon vs. No. 12 Ohio State (Photo by Melinda Meijer/ISI Photos/Getty Images) Spread: Ohio State -7.5 Moneyline: Ohio State -305, Oregon +245 Klatt's thoughts: " Oregon at Ohio State . "This is not the same Ohio State that came into Eugene a couple of years ago and would eventually win the national championship. And it is certainly not the same Ohio State that you saw in the Rose Bowl, and that kind of, you know, blew the hinges off in that game. I don't know what we're going to get. It's like Ohio State's backed into a corner … You just get all of Ohio State, and if you get all of Ohio State, that means that you get all of Jeremiah Smith , and they're going to be taking shots, and they're going to be more aggressive even with a young quarterback, because you got nothing to lose. Cox/Getty Images) Spread: LSU -5.5 Moneyline: LSU -225, Alabama +185 Klatt's thoughts: " Alabama at LSU , always a great game. LSU is favored by 5.5 over the committee's fifth-ranked team. I think it's a terrible matchup for Alabama. Let me tell you why, because if Kalen DeBoer gets into a big game, typically they throw the football a lot and they don't run it very well. Terrific, second in the country in sacks. Meanwhile, you would think that Alabama on the offensive line would do a good job protecting their quarterback. Not the case. So again, all of this leads to: Do I think LSU can at least get out of their own way offensively, not turn the football over and score some points? The answer is yes. Sam Leavitt is playing better. LSU covers the 5.5" Klatt's straight-up pick: LSU Klatt's pick against the spread: LSU -5.5 No. 7 Texas vs. Missouri (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) Spread: Texas -2.5 Moneyline: Texas -142, Missouri +120 Klatt's thoughts: " Texas at Missouri. away.headline: BYU releases initial LJ Martin injury status ahead of Utah game
away.blurb: On Wednesday night, the BYU football program provided the first official injury update for LJ Martin ahead of a top 10 matchup with Utah. Martin is "doubtful" for the game against the Utes. The "doubtful" designation is reserved for the players that have a 25% chance to play. However, just a few minutes before the injury report came out, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Martin is considered "questionable" for this weekend. The "questionable" designation is reserved for players with a 50% chance to play. Thamel reported that if Martin returns, "he's not expected to be 100% and could be limited." Thamel added more information, saying "[Martin is] trending to dress, be available, and have some impact on the game. A final decision will be made later this week." Martin was back practicing on Tuesday, according to Aaron Roderick. The last time he played was in early October against TCU. If Martin can't go, BYU will turn to Preston Rex who was not available for the ASU game. Rex had a breakout game against Notre Dame before suffering an injury against UCF. If Saleapaga isn't available, expect more sets with three wide receivers. That would leave Walker Lyons on the field for most of the game. If Evan Johnson can't play, BYU will turn to Jayven Williams and Therrian Alexander III at cornerback. Williams and Alexander shut down two of the best wide receivers in the Big 12 last week. They are more than capable of holding it down on the outside. The bigger question will be who BYU plays at nickel. The Cougars started Cannon DeVries at that spot to start the season, but DeVries has primarily been used for punt return duties since he suffered an injury. The ASU game was the first time DeVries had seen defensive snaps since suffering the injury. He played 14 snaps. LJ Martin and Evan Johnson Officially Ruled Out for BYU Against ASU If Martin returns, it would be the first time BYU has had its full compliment of running backs since the season opener. Other Injury Updates on BYU Starters BYU also provided injury updates on key starters Roger Saleapaga and Evan Johnson. Saleapaga left the game against ASU with an injury, and Johnson suffered what appeared to be a serious ankle injury against UCF. Johnson did not play against Arizona State last weekend. Most of the time, BYU had three safeties on the field. BYU averaged 2.7 safeties on the field at a time against ASU. True freshman Kennan Pula has seen his role grow over the last few weeks. He played 24 snaps against the Sun Devils. away.headline: BYU RB LJ Martin Status Up in Air Heading into Utah Game
away.blurb: BYU star running back's status for the Utah game this Saturday is one of the main storylines for the game. After Martin suffered a leg injury early in the TCU game October 3, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that LJ Martin would be out 4-6 weeks. Five weeks later, Thamel reported Wednesday night that Martin is cleared to practice and is "questionable" to return. From Thamel: "Sources: BYU star tailback LJ Martin is considered questionable to return Saturday against No. 3 Utah. He's cleared to practice and has been available this week. If he's back, he's not expected to be 100-percent and could be limited. He's trending to dress, be available and have some impact on the game. A final decision will be made later in the week. Martin has been out since Oct. 3, and BYU beat Notre Dame without him in the line-up. He's the 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year." BYU released its initial availability report Wednesday, and Martin is listed as doubtful. Cornerback Evan Johnson, who missed the Arizona State game, and Tight End Roger Saleapaga are also listed as doubtful. BYU will have RB Preston Rex back, who missed the Arizona State game, but getting LJ back in some capacity versus Utah would certainly helped. BYU's running back room has struggled since LJ went down, and even a limited LJ would give the running game some extra juice and put little less pressure on Bear in both the run and pass game. Texas' defense will stiffen in the red zone against a strong Missouri run game, and Arch Manning will continue to churn yards on the ground in a grinding, just-effective-enough afternoon for the Longhorns' offense. picks.blurb: No. 7 Texas vs. No. 18 Missouri preview: Tigers host Longhorns for top 25 battle | Burnt Orange Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Texas Longhorns Community Burnt Orange Nation November 5, 2026 Burnt Orange Nation Notifications Notifications Get The App Sections Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Texas Football Odds Texas Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search Get The App Sections Expand Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications Texas Longhorns Football A balanced Tiger team hosts the Longhorns for a top-25 matchup on Saturday. Boasting a 6-2 record and Top 25 ranking, the No. 19 Missouri Tigers host the No. 7 Texas Longhorns this Saturday in a matchup with huge implications for both teams. With identical records overall and in conference play, this matchup will be a reality check for postseason expectations for both squads. Win, and the path to the playoffs remain wide open. Lose, and the rest of the season could be tough to overcome. Missouri began the season with a 3-0 record that included a win over rival Kansas, but then fell at the hands of Mississippi State 31-24 in a close battle on the road. The Tigers bounced back with a 45-17 thrashing of Florida and a 27-6 win over Texas A&M. With a 5-1 record, Missouri was starting to get national attention. However, Ole Miss pumped the brakes on that narrative in a 31-3 victory. The Tigers failed to score on any drive after the opening series and elite running back Jamal Roberts was held to less than two yards per carry on 20 touches. The Rebel defense also forced quarterback Austin Simmons to throw 44 passes, a formula that Muschamp will likely seek to repeat. The Tigers bounced back last week with a 34-10 win over Arkansas while forcing four turnovers. Missouri brings a stingy defense and talented offense to the table. The Tigers rank fifth in the SEC in scoring defense, one spot behind the Longhorns, while their rushing and passing attacks both slot at sixth or better. Texas has the defensive personnel to make Missouri struggle, but limiting quarterback Austin Simmons and running back Jamal Roberts will not be easy. The Tigers also boast the most productive wide receivers in the conference in Cayden Lee. The Longhorn defense has to plug the run game, something that the Tigers rely on heavily. On the other side of the ball, Texas will need to win through the air. Missouri gives up less than 100 yards per game on the ground, a stellar number, but can be susceptible through the air. They’ve been able to create turnovers, so winning that battle will also be crucial. No matter how you spin it, this matchup will require a strong showing from Texas. Missouri took a step back last season but appears poised to return to the success they found under head coach Eli Drinkwitz in 2023 and 2024. Now in his seventh season, Drinkwitz has Missouri on the doorstep of competing with the traditional powers in the SEC. His offensive background has flourished in recent years, including this one, and the team has shown to be a resilient bunch with impressive wins after both losses. Here’s how the Tigers stack up position by position. The Tiger offense has been remarkably efficient this season and features one of the best running backs in the country in Jamal Roberts, the engine of the offense and that allows quarterback Austin Simmons to find ample space down the field. Stopping the fourth best run game in the SEC and making the offense one dimensional will be a key for the Longhorn defense. Quarterback Austin Simmons leads the offense for the Tigers. The transfer quarterback is in his first season with Missouri after spending three years in Oxford with Ole Miss. He’s taken a winding road to this season that began as a dual-sport athlete. Originally expected to be a member of the 2025 high school class, Simmons reclassified to 2023, ending his high school career two years early to pursue both football and baseball as the Division 1 level. He took classes year round and completed an associate degrees at age 17 with an impressive GPA, giving him the academic credentials necessary to enroll two years ahead of schedule. As a Rebel, Simmons sat behind NY Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart before taking over the starting job in 2025. An ankle injury forced him to miss time which gave current Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss the chance to start, a role he never relinquished. Simmons transferred this past offseason. With great size and an accurate lefty motion, Simmons has put together a clean campaign this year. He’s completed 152-of-240 passes (63.3 percent) for 16 touchdowns and most importantly, just two interceptions. This season, he’s been feast or famine despite the efficiency, throwing for 290 yards or more in four contests but less than 180 in three others. Simmons isn’t particularly dangerous as a runner. He’s best working off play action, so stopping the run game and forcing him into obvious passing situations will help limit his effectiveness. Heading into the season, first-team All-American Ahmad Hardy was expected to continue his dominant 2025 season. An emergency surgery in the offseason due to a gunshot wound at a concert forced Hardy to miss the beginning of the season, but the star returned last week for the first time, carrying the ball twice for five yards. He’s still reaching 100-percent health, but is expected to get some handoffs on Saturday. Hardy’s absence opened the door for Roberts, who leads the SEC in rush yards per game and ranks third in the FBS with 1,005 yards. Roberts was an impressive second option last season, tallying 753 yards on 124 carries, and has taken full advantage of Hardy being sidelined. He put up 211 yards against Florida and followed it up the next week with 222 against A&M. Roberts will see a healthy dose of carries, likely somewhere around 25, as well as a few passes out of the backfield. He can turn a routine play into extra yards with his physical running style and break off huge runs with his acceleration and top end speed. Shutting him down is the biggest task for the Texas defense and arguably one of the most important factors of the game. Wide receiver Missouri’s offense is run centric, but features Cayden Lee, the most productive wide receiver in the SEC. He spent three seasons in Oxford with Simmons before the duo elected to transfer to Missouri together. What a recruiting win that turned out to be for Drinkwitz. Lee is electric. At 5’11, 180 pounds, Lee isn’t a huge target. However, he has a great feel for finding space and creating explosive plays from the slot. He converts first downs and catches everything, making him an extremely reliable receiver. He’s leading the SEC with 756 yards receiving and second in catches with 53. The other wide receiver to know is sophomore Donovan Olugbode. A bigger target at 6’2, 210 pounds, Olugbode has reeled in 40 catches for 584 yards and seven touchdowns in seven games. He missed the A&M game in early October, but returned to catch nine passes for 127 yards against Ole Miss, as well as a touchdown last week. Solely bracketing Lee is not possible with what Olugbode can do. Each requires attention, and can wreck a secondary, especially when the run game pulls extra defenders to the line of scrimmage. The tight end for the Tigers is senior Brett Norfleet, who has impressive size at 6’6, 255 pounds, and has recorded nine catches for 80 yards and a touchdown this season. He’s an experienced player with 1,400+ snaps in the past three seasons. Offensive line The Missouri offensive line has been solid this year, creating holes for Roberts and time for Simmons. This group was forced to replace three of the five starters, but has hardly missed a beat this year. Leading the way is 2025 first-team All-SEC left tackle Cayden Green, one of the conference’s best bookends. He’s joined by a host of other reliable options that have experience and talent. This group rarely gives up sacks and has imposed their will against every team other than Ole Miss. It is one of the best the Longhorns will face all season. The Missouri offense is capable across the board. It starts up front with a reliable front five that has allowed Roberts to establish himself as one of the best in the country. His success has opened space in the secondary and the play-action offense, giving Simmons room to operate. He’s got two skilled wide receivers to throw to, creating a well-balanced unit that has performed well this season. The Tigers struggled against Ole Miss, a formula that Texas will undoubtedly look to recreate on Saturday. Missouri’s defense has arguably been the more consistent unit. It has been extremely effective against the run and generated turnovers at a high rate. It ranks top 30 in the country in many areas and has looked salty, excluding the Ole Miss game. However, the secondary has given up yards through the air, meaning this game could fall on the shoulders of the offensive line creating time and Manning delivering accurate passes. Defensive line Leading the way up the middle are Marquis Gracial and Jalen Marshall. Gracial tallied 257 snaps for Missouri in 2025 and has been effective against the run. Marshall bring great size at 6’4, 335 pounds and experience. He saw 342 snaps last year. Donta Simpson is another guy coming off injury that will provide a presence inside. The group of defensive ends is strong. A trio of Daeden Hopkins, Darris Smith, and Langdon Kitchen give Missouri depth to keep fresh legs. Hopkins shined brightest earlier in the season with 6.5 sacks in his first three games, but has since cooled off and will come off the bench. Smith is coming off an injury and saw his highest snap count in a month last week. He recorded three hurries and recovered a fumble last week. This unit has been hurt by injuries but can still get after it. They’re effective against the run and have depth that brings talent off the bench. The Missouri linebacker duo is made up by junior Nicholas Rodriguez and senior Robert Woodyard Jr. Rodriguez came into the season as the most veteran linebacker on the team after playing 352 snaps last season, which was the third most on the team. He was graded as a highly-effective run stopper according to Pro Football Focus — 86.4 run defense and 78.4 tackling. This season, he’s leading the tram with 88 tackles, 20 more than the next closest. He’s also added four quarterback hits and two forced fumbles. Next to him, Woodyard has emerged as another transfer recruiting win for Drinkwitz. After spending three seasons at Auburn, Woodyard opted to keep his mascot the same but suit up in black and gold instead. He’s been a much needed addition to the Missouri defense, posting 49 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, an interception, and forced fumble. Rodriguez is the centerpiece of this unit and the defense as a whole. He’s active and productive. Texas should test these two with screens and misdirection early in the game, something opposing offenses have keyed on. The cornerback position was hit hard this offseason and forced to replace three starters from last season. To combat the lack of experience, Missouri turned to the portal bringing in a host of players to compete for the starting jobs. Fifth-year transfer Chris Graves secured one of the spots after starting nine games for Ole Miss last season while Sione Laulea, who spent last season with Oregon, will see most of the snaps at the other spot. Both possess good size. Graves brings much more experience than anyone else on the backend and arrived with Simmons and Lee. Another corner to know is Jahlil Florence, a physical corner who has been unable to play much the last few seasons due to injury. Multiple first-round picks are set to miss this game, and it's a perfect storm for the Tigers. The one thing that has me thinking Missouri can win is quarterback Austin Simmons. He can attack every blade of grass and has a real chance to be a top pick in the NFL Draft. I'll give the Tigers a win over the Longhorns. Missouri 23, Texas 20: Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee This SHOULD be a playoff elimination game, with both teams coming into this game with two losses. They beat Ohio State and Ole Miss at home, two excellent wins, but they lost to a terrible Oklahoma team in Dallas and lost to Florida at home. I trust Missouri's run game more than I trust Texas' offense, which totaled just 280 yards last week in a comfortable win over Mississippi State. Jamal Roberts is third in the nation in rushing yards and has gone for 138+ in three of his last four games with two 200+ yard games in that span. With the Tigers' ground game and the home field advantage, it's just enough for Mizzou to pick up a massive win. Already without starting left tackle Trevor Goosby for the remainder of the season, the injury issues have piled up for Texas headed into Saturday's road matchup with the Missouri Tigers. Now, the Longhorns are receiving worst-case scenario news when it comes to starting running back Hollywood Smothers, who exited last week's game against Mississippi State with an apparent lower-body injury. Smothers will miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a torn MCL in his knee, according to multiple reports. He started the year off as the team's starter after transferring in from NC State. In the second half against Mississippi State, Smothers took a hard hit to his lower body and sat on the turf holding his left knee. He was then helped off the field by trainers and was unable to put any weight on his left leg. Smothers finishes his 2026 season with 69 carries for 283 yards and two touchdowns along with 10 catches for 79 yards and another score. His pair of rushing touchdowns came in one of the biggest moments of Texas' season, as he had two scores in the fourth quarter against Ohio State, highlighted by the game-winning touchdown in the final minute to complete the comeback. The Longhorns have already gotten accustomed to life without Smothers this season. He previously dealt with ankle and shoulder injuries, forcing him to miss games against Tennessee and Ole Miss. Texas running back Raleek Brown now becomes the no-doubt starter moving forward for the Longhorns. So far this season, he's tallied 92 carries for 452 yards and five touchdowns along with 12 catches for 54 yard and another score. This was highlighted by an impressive performance in the win over Ole Miss when he had 23 carries for 157 yards. Behind him, Michael Terry III and Derrek Cooper will continue to receive an uptick in snaps. Terry has impressed and appears to have overtaken Cooper on the depth chart. When the Bruins arrive this time, it'll be in the low 40s at kickoff, they'll face a Minnesota team that already has two home upsets this season, and the Gophers' offense will be up against a defense that would rather get a root canal than give up a touchdown. Picking the side takes some nerve. Picking a low-scoring game doesn't. Bob Chesney's first season in Westwood has been ridiculous. UCLA is 8-0, ranked fifth and leading the Big Ten, and it's done it largely with a defense run by coordinator Colin Hitschler. The Bruins allow 13.4 points per game (fifth nationally) and 4.1 yards per play (third), and opponents convert only 25.9% of their third downs. Over the last four games, UCLA has allowed 15, 7, 10 and 0 points. The offense changed when Nico Iamaleava tore his ACL at Oregon on Oct. 10. Ty Dieffenbach, a Cal Poly transfer, has been steady since then, but UCLA has become a run-first, clock-killing team. The Bruins scored 17, 28 and 27 in his three starts. Wayne Knight has 680 rushing yards and 12 rushing touchdowns, UCLA averages 219.5 rushing yards per game, and its 33:40 average time of possession ranks fourth nationally. Long drives also tend to stall: UCLA is 110th in red-zone scoring. That adds up to a lot of fourth-quarter field goals. Drake Lindsey threw for 120 yards on 37 attempts in the Indiana loss, and the heat on offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. is turning up. In five of its seven games against FBS opponents, Minnesota has scored 20 points or fewer: 13, 20, 13, 13 and 16. Now it gets a top-five scoring defense. away.headline: UCLA football week 10 injury report: updates, status, replacement options
away.blurb: Rowe was injured in the contest against Nevada a week ago after catching a beautiful sideline grab to move the chains. The positive thing is that Rowe lands as a probable active, giving quarterback Ty Dieffenbach one of his best weapons in the passing game against Minnesota. The Bruins are preparing for one of their toughest matchups of the season as they hit the road and travel to Minneapolis to take on the 5-3 Minnesota Golden Gophers. As the Bruins prepare for the final leg of their season, it's crucial they don't slip up and continue to bolster their resume to get a shot at the College Football Playoff. In the Week 10 conference matchup, the Bruins will be without some key players, as the initial availability report was released ahead of the contest. Rodrick Pleasant, Defensive Back Ryan McCulloch, Outside Linebacker Of course, the Bruins will be without the usuals, as some players have already suffered season-ending injuries this season, which have been major losses for UCLA's offense. Ashton Sanders and Ryan McCulloch will both be sidelined in the matchup, which could be a loss to keep an eye on if Minnesota’s running game can do some damage. This will be the second straight week that the Bruins will be without Davis, who has arguably been their best offensive lineman this season. In order to beat the Golden Gophers, UCLA will need to get their ground game to produce as we saw at the beginning of the season, and Davis would have played a huge part in that success. Without him in the starting lineup, it could create more of a reliance on Ty Dieffenbach to deliver the ball well through the air. UCLA has had injuries pile up all season throughout the wide receiver room, and the latest Bruin landing on the injury report is speedster Brian Rowe. While the Bruins will be without many talented players on their roster, Bob Chesney and the Bruins have been able to overcome every bumps in the road so far this season. UCLA will need everybody to play their part if they want to extend the win streak and advance to 9-0 on the road. A team which Alabama has won the last three games against dating back to 2023, this latest showdown against LSU is likely to be their toughest in recent years. The Tigers are considered one of the SEC's top teams at 6-2 (3-2 SEC), and have a roster loaded with talent led by head coach Lane Kiffin. In addition to that, this latest matchup between the Crimson Tide and Tigers has significant College Football Playoff (CFP) implications. Released this past Tuesday night, Alabama was ranked No. 5 in the first CFP rankings as the top ranked two-loss team, while LSU sat at No. 14. A challenging matchup, let's make three predictions for the Crimson Tide during Saturday's massive road game at LSU. picks.blurb: Alabama Given Shocking Prediction Ahead of LSU Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Alabama Given Shocking Prediction Ahead of LSU Showdown (David Leong-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:01 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Alabama Crimson Tide will be heading out on the road to take on the LSU Tigers this weekend, in what could be the biggest game on the schedule. Both Alabama and LSU come into the game with a record of 6-2, giving each team a chance to make a real statement . Each team is coming off a bye week, giving them more rest and time to prepare for this huge game. With SEC schedule changes coming, this matchup will be the last one played between the two teams on a yearly basis. This could add more emphasis for both sides to want to come away with the win. With this rivalry game kicking off in a few days, the Crimson Tide aren't being favored to come away with the win on the road. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Alabama only has a 43 percent chance of taking down LSU this week. Since the game is being played on the road, LSU is likely being favored, especially since Tiger Stadium can be so tough to play in. One of the bigger keys to the game for the Crimson Tide will be how quarterback Keelon Russell can perform. Alabama has all the confidence in the world in Russell, but he has been a little shaky at times this season. For the year, the signal-caller has thrown for 2,057 yards with 15 touchdowns and five interceptions through the air. On the ground, Russell has made his presence known for this team, rushing for Russell has proven to be very impactful for Alabama, even with his limited experience as a starting quarterback. If Russell can handle the hostile atmosphere that LSU will throw at him, the Crimson Tide could have a strong chance to win the game. Alabama is going to need Russell to play more like he did against Kentucky earlier in the season, rather than how he looked against Tennessee a few weeks ago. The signal-caller have a lot of talent, but he can sometimes make poor decisions with the football. LSU has a very strong defense, and this will be a major challenge for Russell to overcome this week. But if Alabama is going to reach the heights that this program wants to get to this season, Russell is going to have to be able to handle these types of games. Kickoff for the final yearly meeting between the two rivals is set for 12:30 p.m. PT/3:30 p.m. ET from Baton Rouge.

The loser of this game may miss out on the college football playoff and given the Tigers' remaining strength of schedule, this is a must-win for LSU. Both teams are coming off a bye week, so we should expect a chess match between Lane Kiffin and Kalen DeBoer . Some would say this is a must-win for Alabama despite being the #5 ranked team in the new playoff rankings. The Tide's two best wins came against Kentucky when the Wildcats were unranked and a routing of #16 Mississippi State which sent Kamario Taylor and the program into a spiral. A win at LSU would solidify Alabama's spot, but a loss puts their season in the hands of others. Alabama plays Vanderbilt, Chattanooga, and Auburn following LSU; one of the easiest strength of schedules in P4. Alabama trailed 20-17 to Texas A&M before rattling off 14 points in the fourth quarter to avoid three-straight losses. Keelon Russell threw for 311 yards and three touchdowns, and the defense forced three turnovers in the win. Alabama has won three straight against LSU and won 12 of the last 15. Sam Leavitt and Kiffin will try to break the streak in his debut season. LSU is coming off two back-to-back big wins before the bye week. The Tigers crushed Mississippi State 31-0 and Auburn 38-17. Sam Leavitt threw seven touchdowns and ran for another in that two-game span, plus Jackson Harris caught four of those touchdowns and totaled 263 receiving yards. LSU's defense has only allowed 281 yards through the air in those two games as well, so nothing should come easy in Death Valley for one of the best home defenses in the country. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Alabama has been without Ryan Coleman-Williams for the last two games (TENN, TX A&M), but he could return this week, which would significantly boost Russell's output. Woodson has four games with double-digit tackles this season after having one in three seasons with Virginia Tech. Jackson Harris has also caught four touchdowns and put up 263 yards in the last two games, so the stars have been shining for LSU. LSU Player to Watch on Offense: QB Sam Leavitt Sam Leavitt might be playing his best football of the season. In the last two games, Leavitt has thrown seven passing touchdowns with no picks and a rushing touchdown. In his first six games of the season, he had at least one pick in all of them, so this is a pleasant surprise for LSU. Leavitt has 25 total touchdowns on the year (17 pass, 8 rush) and will be a handful in this game with his dual-threat ability. Alabama has only allowed two quarterbacks to throw for two-plus touchdowns on their defense this season, and Leavitt has accomplished that in five straight games. If LSU wants to win, Leavitt will have to be on his A-game, and he went into the bye week on fire. LSU has only forced one turnover in that dominant two-game stretch, and the Tigers will likely need to win the turnover battle to beat Alabama. LSU's defense ranks fifth in pressure and first in coverage grades per PFF, and with the Tide ranking 54th in pass blocking, LSU could find success getting to Keelon Russell . LSU Player to Watch on Defense: DE Princewill Umanmielen Princewill Umanmielen got back in this sack column against Auburn! picks.headline: ‘If they don't get time, it's going to be a real uphill climb' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs LSU
picks.blurb: ‘If they don't get time, it's going to be a real uphill climb' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs LSU - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Zach Ragan · AtoZ Sports Tue, November 3, 2026 at 8:43 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The LSU Tigers will host the Alabama Crimson Tide in a huge SEC showdown in Baton Rouge this weekend. LSU will host Alabama this upcoming Saturday in what's a de facto College Football Playoff elimination game. Alabama and LSU both have two losses. It's possible that the loser of this game could still get into the playoff with three losses — it depends on how the rest of the season plays out — but the winner will be the only one that controls its own destiny moving forward. ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, made his score prediction for the game, and he has LSU leaving Tiger Stadium with a 27-20 win. McElroy thinks LSU's defensive line will be able to win the battle up front. "I'm taking LSU to win the game 27-20," said McElroy. "I do think the under is in play, but it's really going to come down to Alabama's offensive line. If Keelon Russell gets time, they can win this game in Baton Rouge. But if they don't get time, it's going to be a real uphill climb for the Crimson Tide." McElroy noted that most of the sacks Alabama has given up this season have come from Russell holding the ball too long. Alabama and LSU will kick off at 2:30 PM CT/3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Eight teams are 3-2 or better in conference play, 3-3 South Carolina and Florida teams are ranked in the College Football Playoff top 24, and four other teams are dangerous in an Any Given Saturday sort of way. Alabama is 4-2 in the SEC and 6-2 overall, 6-2 LSU is 3-2 in the conference, and for the winner, it's able to stay alive for another week. The loser won't be dead in the CFP and SEC chases, but its season will be on life support. Beyond that, it's Lane Kiffin – who maybe, probably, could've and should've been the Alabama head coach after Nick Saban retired – and his loaded LSU team going against an explosive, but flawed, Crimson Tide squad that has the minerals to rip through the CFP if it can get there. Alabama vs LSU: Quick Hits LSU is 14th in the first CFP rankings. After this, it hosts Texas before closing at Tennessee and at Arkansas. Alabama started out fifth in the first CFP rankings. It goes to Vanderbilt after this before hosting Chattanooga to get ready for the Auburn game. Alabama has won the last three meetings and, starting with the 2011 national title, has won 13 of the last 15. How To Watch Alabama vs LSU Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Alabama Will Win How do you beat this LSU team? You throw, you keep throwing, and you counter every big moment by the Tigers with an even bigger moment coming through the air. Trinidad Chambliss threw 48 times for 363 yards in the 32-24 Ole Miss win over the Tigers. Kenny Minchey wasn't always on in Kentucky's 35-34 win over LSU, but he threw 36 times for 246 yards. No one else has been able to throw more than 30 passes against LSU, partly because the Tiger offense is usually in total control. Alabama doesn't always have to dominate the narrative, but when its offense starts rolling, it comes in waves. From the fourth quarter in the 31-20 win over Texas A&M, to the 35-3 first half against South Carolina, to scoring 29 unanswered points in the win over Kentucky, when quarterback Keelon Russell and the Tide attack find a groove, look out. But LSU is all about the momentum. When it's going downhill on both sides of the ball, this looks and plays like the fastest and most dangerous team going. That starts with the run defense that swarms around everything, keeping teams to under three yards per carry. The Tigers allowed multiple touchdown runs three times, and all three games were on the road, including the two losses. "They're not all in the exact same spot, but they're all out there going through workouts. Some are taking team reps, some are taking non-contact reps. "But I think the progress by all of them is headed in a good direction. We'll see. I think a lot of it has to do with how their bodies respond after they're out there being pushed a little bit more." Will Sanders: lower-extremity – sustained against Texas A&M and is out for a couple of weeks "Guys are making good progress," DeBoer said. "I think that's what a lot of it was said on Monday. A lot of guys out there going through practice. I know a lot of that report will be coming out here, as we have to do with the SEC report." LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 12 Ohio State hosts No. 23 Oregon in a pivotal game in the Big Ten and CFP race Getty Images Week 10 of the college football calendar has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Oregon live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Ohio Stadium -- Columbus, Ohio TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium Ohio State vs. Oregon prediction, picks The Ducks have to pick up where they left off offensively to have a chance here, and they should push the tempo a bit and try to stretch things out in the air. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. picks.blurb: Oregon Ducks’ Playoff Odds Offer A Twist Before Ohio State Skip to main content SI.COM Transfer Portal FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2024 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM DUCKS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM DUCKS BB The Oregon Ducks are rolling into their premier matchup against the No. 11 Ohio State Buckeyes with momentum. Oregon took down another AP Top-25 team, the No. 20 Northwestern Wildcats, and finally found an offensive rhythm. But the 34-26 win doesn’t change the fact that a 6-2 Buckeyes squad vs. a 5-3 Ducks team presents a much different matchup than their No. 1 and No. 2 preseason rankings suggested. While Ohio State’s postseason ambitions are still alive, Oregon’s three losses may not have eliminated it yet, at least according to the ESPN Football Power Ranking (FPI). Oregon Ducks coach Dan Lanning | Darby Winter Oregon Ducks’ College Football Playoff Hopes Not Dead Yet Oregon Ducks’ College Football Playoff Hopes Not Dead Yet The Ducks are No. 12 in the Week 10 ESPN FPI. The FPI still gives Oregon a chance, albeit a low one, to make the College Football Playoff at 4.2 percent. Additionally, Oregon is provided a 2.8 percent chance to win the Big Ten, a 0.4 percent chance to make the National Championship and a 0.2 percent chance to win the National Championship. What’s notable about the FPI is that its favorable ranking of Oregon, even with the turbulent first two months of the season, could still set the Ducks up for a postseason berth if the committee sees it the same way. After all, the 2026 college football season has already featured a plethora of twists and turns. Oregon defensive lineman Matayo Uiagalelei | Darby Winter The No. 5 UCLA Bruins and the No. 6 Indiana Hoosiers are the only two teams in the Big Ten with less than two loses. Oregon would need to win out and hope that a few other games outside its control go its way. The No. 5 UCLA Bruins and the No. 6 Indiana Hoosiers are the only two teams in the Big Ten with less than two loses. Oregon would need to win out and hope that a few other games outside its control go its way. The Ducks’ strength of schedule appears to give them the benefit of the doubt. Every Oregon opponent so far, except the Portland State Vikings, is ranked within the top 50 of the ESPN FPI. Five of the Ducks’ first eight opponents have also been ranked inside the Top 25 at some point in 2026. So the chances of the Ducks playing anything besides a bowl game in December might seem like a pipe dream, but if the selection committee sees it the same way as the FPI, it's not impossible. Either way, it adds to the stakes of the upcoming game in Columbus. Big Ohio State Buckeyes Matchup on the Horizon The Buckeyes narrowly lost a 24-23 battle against the Texas Longhorns on Sept. 12 but bounced back in dominant fashion. It seemed that Ohio State was going to be a difficult team to beat a second time down the stretch of the season, especially after defeating the Hoosiers 19-15. But an unranked USC Trojans team that just came off an upset loss against the Wisconsin Badgers continued the chaos in the Big Ten by taking down the Buckeyes 30-18. Ohio State now enters the game against Oregon in a similar situation the Ducks were in after losing to the Bruins – a loss could end its hopes of returning to the CFP. The Buckeyes still have games against Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan left on the schedule. The Ducks’ only two wins against the Buckeyes come in the last two regular season meetings, with last one at Autzen Stadium and the 2021 meeting in Columbus. Ohio State did, however, get the best of the Ducks the last time out in a 41-21 victory in the 2025 Rose Bowl. Ohio State at home, coming off its second loss of the season, is a dangerous matchup, but Oregon now has the opportunity to play spoiler for other teams' postseason desires. Though freshman Luke Fahey has operated as the starter during Ohio State's bye week and loss to USC last week, OSU is still adjusting to life without its starting signal-caller. That's a huge advantage for an Oregon team that has settled in on its starter moving forward in Dylan Raiola and seemed to find its identity on offense in a win versus Northwestern. Why Ohio State has an advantage: No one has had an answer for Ohio State superstar and future NFL top-10 pick Jeremiah Smith. The junior has 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns in eight games and is already the Big Ten's all-time leader in touchdown receptions in less than three seasons of play. Stopping Smith will be a massive challenge for the Ducks , who have shown to be susceptible against the passing game at points this season. Oregon vs. Ohio State injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports were made public. For Oregon: Several key Oregon contributors could return this week, though Lanning wouldn't talk about the specific status of any player during his Monday press conference and deferred to the Ducks' upcoming availability reports. Starting running back Jordon Davison was hobbled in the first half against Northwestern and was seen with crutches on the sideline in the second half, though Lanning said he didn't expect the injury to be long-term. For Ohio State: The biggest injury news for the Buckeyes revolves around Sayin, who is out for the foreseeable future since an injury versus Indiana in mid-October. Ohio State was also without standout freshman DB Jay Timmons and talented wideout Brandon Inniss vs. USC. Inniss was a game-time decision and participated in early warmups but did not play against the Trojans.
