Oregon vs. Ohio State: 4 bold predictions Oregon, Ohio State first half will be a defensive battle The Ducks rediscovered a bit of their old selves in a 38-point outing against a stout Northwestern defense last week, but the challenge will be greater this week, and the Ducks have yet to put together back-to-back good performances against good competition this season. That needs to change Saturday, but both teams, adjusting to new schemes and personnel, will get off to a slow start in Columbus this weekend. Ducks will hold Buckeyes' Jeremiah Smith under 100 yards Oregon has a good history of limiting opposing stars, though sometimes to a fault. Last season against future NFL draftee Makai Lemon and USC, the star had just 34 yards on seven catches in an Oregon win. But, that left Tanook Hines with the opportunity to cash in on the attention Lemon received. Lanning and his staff will have Smith circled everywhere, and they'll hold Smith under 100 yards, but Ohio State will still get production from other talents. Ohio State, Oregon game will come to down to field position, turnovers As most games do, Saturday's contest will come down to who commits more mistakes and who takes advantage of good field position. On the former front, Oregon has struggled mightily with protecting the ball. The Ducks have given the ball away 13 times this season, including 10 fumbles, while Ohio State has protected the ball slightly better but produces less turnovers on defense. Oregon punter Bailey Ettridge has been a massive weapon throughout the season, and if he can continually pin the Buckeyes deep, Oregon will have a good chance to spring the upset. Ahead of the key Big Ten battle in Week 10, the college football staff has predictions on how Ohio State vs. Oregon is going to shake out. Ohio State 27, Oregon 20 The Buckeyes losing in Week 9 to USC stung so bad because it wasn't Julian Sayin's absence and starting a true freshman that did it. Luke Fahey played well enough to win that game and the rest of the team was a letdown for the most part. Ryan Day said everyone had to step up a little bit with a true freshman playing, but the opposite happened, with regression taking place. Flash forward a week and Ohio State's defense needs to get back on track against an Oregon team that's going to rely on its playmakers through the air. Dylan Raiola is going to get the ball to Dakorien Moore and tight end Jamari Johnson. Ohio State can't allow explosives as they did against USC, or it'll be another upset. I think Ohio State is going to respond at home in a way where they control this one the majority of the way, and fans feel a bit more at ease. - Brandon Little, A to Z Sports Ohio State Ohio State 27, Oregon 17 I'm taking Ohio State to defeat Oregon 27-17 in a matchup that has lost some of its luster, especially with both teams turning to backup quarterbacks. Still, I think the Buckeyes have a significant advantage defensively and will make life difficult for Oregon throughout the afternoon. Ohio State should be able to generate pressure, force some uncomfortable decisions and come up with several big plays that swing momentum. On the other side, freshman quarterback Luke Fahey shows some encouraging signs of growth. He won't be spectacular, but I expect him to look more comfortable and give Buckeye fans some reasons for optimism moving forward. Dylan Raiola will have his moments, making a few impressive throws and creating some explosive plays to keep Oregon within striking distance. However, the Ducks won't be able to find enough consistency offensively to keep pace. Ohio State's defense ultimately makes the difference, coming up with timely stops when Oregon needs answers most. Fahey does enough to help the Buckeyes put points on the board, and Ohio State controls the closing stages to secure a relatively comfortable win.- Ryan Roberts, A to Z Sports Notre Dame Ohio State 17, Oregon 16 Simply put, Ohio State is a much better team, but they aren't nearly good enough as of yet without Julian Sayin. The Ducks aren't doing much better, either, especially with Dante Moore not playing. The Ducks are reeling on multiple fronts, and Dan Lanning has many quesitoning his job performance. That will continue, as the Buckeyes find a way to win a dogfight. - Tyler Forness, A to Z Sports Florida Ohio State 20, Oregon 16 This is a very tough game to get a handle on, as both teams are riding with backup quarterbacks. Dylan Raiola bounced back last weekend against Northwestern looking more like the QB that helped the Ducks beat USC in Los Angeles. Speaking of LA, the Buckeyes struggled with Luke Fahey under center in a 30-18 loss to the Trojans. Jeremiah Smith did manage to log 10 catches, but he turned them into 83 yards and a touchdown, a relatively pedestrian total for him. This is a game that's an ugly offensive slog for much of the afternoon. Despite winning 34-26, the Ducks struggled against the run last week against the Wildcats, allowing 175 yards. Two weeks ago, Illinois went for 225 against Dan Lanning's team. The Buckeyes ran the ball well last week against USC with 204 rushing yards. The passing games don't work well for either team, but you can stamp US Mail on Bo Jackson and the OSU ground game on Saturday, which does just enough to eek out a close win. - Craig Smith, A to Z Sports Miami Ohio State 25, Oregon 15 This game is the season for the Ohio State Buckeyes. After losing quarterback Julian Sayin, a lot of people expected a big drop-off in Luke Fahey, but he was the last of the Buckeyes' problems last week against USC. The problem for Oregon is, they have been one of the biggest disappointments in the sport. Even before the season-ending injury to Dante Moore, the team was getting whooped in the trenches, and the coordinator changes fell flat. Now there are more questions than answers at quarterback, and they have to travel to Columbus to take on a Buckeyes team with their backs against the wall. That's a recipe for disaster for the Ducks in my opinion. The Buckeyes figure it out and start their win streak on Saturday. - Rob Gregson, A to Z Sports Alabama Ohio State 24, Oregon 17 I think Ohio State can still find a way to win this one, even with the situation they're currently in. The defense will handle the issues that Oregon creates for itself on offense. - Justin Churchill, A to Z Sports Oklahoma This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. home.headline: Ohio State football coach Ryan Day provides promising Julian Sayin injury update
home.blurb: Sayin injured his throwing arm while taking a sack in the fourth quarter against the Hoosiers. Postgame, Day said the Buckeyes expected Sayin to be out several weeks. The following week, Sayin was ruled out “indefinitely” and Day said Ohio State had a plan for Sayin not returning this season or postseason. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State football has been without quarterback Julian Sayin since he was injured in an Oct. 17 win at Indiana. While the Buckeyes could be without Sayin for the remainder of the 2026 season, coach Ryan Day provided a promising update on the junior quarterback Thursday. “All things considered — the outcome with different options that we were kind of going into the situation thinking it could be — I think this has been a decent outcome for us and for him,” Day said on his radio show. “We’ll let him kind of go through that. But this thing looks to be healing. “It’s not going to be next week or next month. It’s going to take some time, but I think certainly for the long term, we feel like we’re on a good track here.” Sayin went back to his home state of California after the injury. He was on Ohio State’s sideline in a sling during Saturday’s loss at USC, often sitting beside freshman quarterback Luke Fahey — the Buckeyes’ new starter. Day said Sayin returned to Columbus after the loss, has been active in helping Fahey and has participated in meetings. “I think it’s important for him to be around the guys,” Day said. “I think it says a lot about him that he’s not just off doing his rehab or whatever. He’s with the team, and he takes his role very seriously.” ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

home.headline: More details emerge about Ohio State QB Julian Sayin and his injury
home.blurb: So, we were left to wonder how long Sayin would be out, with the timeline being deemed "indefinitely." And while many took that to mean the rest of the season, we didn't really know, and still don't to this day. “The guys came out of the game feeling like, ‘OK, we can go on a run with this quarterback here,’” Day said of Fahey. “But we got to go do it, got to go play, got to take the next step.” That's a good thing too, because there's little room for error for Ohio State going forward after it showed up as the No. 12 team in the first release of the 2026 College Football Playoff rankings Tuesday night. The Buckeyes will likely have to win out in the regular season, and it all starts with the game against Oregon at home Saturday. However, according to a report from Bill Rabinowitz of the Dispatch, and some comments from Day on radio Thursday, we now have a little more knowledge of the situation. Not a crystal-clear prognosis by any means, but at least a little something more to go by. According to Rabinowitz (subscription may be required), who spoke to sources close to the program, Sayin suffered a fractured elbow in the fourth quarter against Indiana and had a procedure almost two weeks ago to help repair it, including the insertion of plates and screws. And while that sounds like a long-term thing, and one can hardly classify it as a short-term bump or bruise, it appears as though Sayin's recovery may be ahead of schedule, or at least going along better than some of the alternatives. “All things considered, the outcome with different options that we were kind of going into the situation thinking it could be, I think this has been a decent outcome for us and for him,” Day said on his radio show. “And so we'll let him kind of go through that. But this thing looks to be healing. It's not gonna be next week or next month; it's gonna take some time, but I think certainly for the long term, we feel like we're on a good track here.” It still sounds like Sayin will be shelved for the rest of the year, and that the team is going to have to find a way to play as well as it can with freshman Luke Fahey running the show. Things didn't look great with the team against USC , but Day said the team and coaches feel confident about being able to win with Fahey. In the long history of this rivalry, there's a good case that this is the biggest game ever. In his first year on the job, Will Stein has led Kentucky to a 7-1 start and a great shot at reaching the College Football Playoff with just four games remaining. His major transfer portal additions -- particularly quarterback Kenny Minchey and the offensive line -- clicked almost immediately. To this point, the Wildcats have passed all but one test they've faced, but the level of difficulty rises this weekend. Kentucky must continue to play clean football if it wants to come away with a win in Knoxville. Tennessee had two weeks to wallow in the "what if" after its three-point loss to South Carolina , but the team has to get back in the saddle this weekend. The Volunteers have the chance to pick up their second top-10 win of the season, which would really boost their CFP rankings. There's no doubt that the Vols have a playoff-caliber defense and running game, but can Josh Heupel fix the passing attack? Tennessee must improve there to reach its ceiling. Here is everything you need to know about this top-15 rivalry matchup in Knoxville. Tennessee vs. Kentucky: Need to know Rare ranked matchup: These teams have met well over 100 times, but this is just the fourth ranked matchup in history. Most recently, Tennessee and Kentucky played a top-25 matchup in 2022, with the Volunteers winning in a blowout. Prior to that, the only times the Vols and Wildcats were ranked simultaneously were in 1950 and 1951. That means there's a very good case for this matchup to be the biggest in the history of this rivalry. Games with stakes in this series usually go the way of Tennessee, but can Stein turn the tables on Saturday night? Kentucky not in the giving spirit: The holidays are approaching quickly, but Kentucky has not been feeling very generous. One of the driving factors behind the Wildcats' success is their incredible plus-13 turnover margin. That ranks first in the SEC and fourth in the entire country. For the first time since 2013, Kentucky has avoided turning the ball over in three consecutive games. If any team can end that streak, it's probably Tennessee, which has a great defense and has forced 14 turnovers in eight games. The Vols just have to protect the ball on offense. Heavy dose of DeSean Bishop : Kentucky defensive coordinator Jay Bateman probably doesn't need my advice, but I would suggest he lock in on Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop. He's been the engine of the Vols offense, and his 957 rushing yards rank sixth in the country. His 12 rushing touchdowns are tied for ninth. Over the last four games, Bishop has averaged 29 carries and 159 yards. If the Wildcats can contain Bishop and force Tennessee to throw the ball, that could be a recipe for success, but only one team has effectively shut Bishop down to this point. Kentucky's offense has been incredibly efficient, and it will pose a real challenge to the Tennessee defense. That said, the first night game in Neyland Stadium will give the Vols an edge on that side of the ball. Offensively, Tennessee leans on Bishop and gets enough out of its passing game to pull away from Kentucky late and cover the one-score spread. The Tennessee Vols are currently on the outside looking in at the 12-team College Football Playoff. Tennessee, which is 6-2 with four games remaining, was ranked No. 13 in the initial CFP rankings. The shocking part of Tennessee's ranking isn't that they were at No. 13 — we expected them to be in that range — it's that they were somehow ranked eight spots behind a two-loss Alabama team that lost by 16 points to the Vols a couple of weeks ago. Nearly everyone in college football media was shocked to see Alabama ranked that many spots ahead of the Vols. Murray, who called Tennessee's game against Arkansas for ESPN earlier this season, has the Vols beating the Wildcats 31-21 on Saturday. picks.headline: Tennessee offense preview: Can Kentucky force the Vols to pass?
picks.blurb: Tennessee offense preview: Can Kentucky force the Vols to pass? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Story by Wildcats Wire Tennessee offense preview: Can Kentucky force the Vols to pass? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Wed, November 4, 2026 at 2:31 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to Knoxville to face off against the #16 Tennessee Volunteers on Saturday night, and both teams are coming off of a bye week. We previewed the Tennessee defense and the big scheme showdown between Will Stein's offense against Jim Knowles' defense. Now we will take a look at the Tennessee offense that has consistently put up points under head coach Josh Heupel. Heupel's offense this year has struggled in some areas, and it has resembled the 2024 offense in a lot of ways. Since becoming the head coach of Tennessee in 2021, Josh Heupel has had his offense scoring a lot of points and he is 5-0 against Kentucky . Mark Stoops and Brad White could not figure out Heupel's up-tempo offense that features extremely wide splits from the wide receivers that creates a light box to run the football. Heupel's offenses are averaging over 40 points per game in this series. It is time to see if the new scheme change that has taken place under Jay Bateman will be more effective in slowing down this scheme. This scheme is creative because the wide splits create light boxes that the Vols will then use their ground game to run into favorable looks. Once Tennessee gets the run game going, they will then take shots down the field on deep option routes. However, this offense is similar to the 2024 version, which has become heavily dependent on the run game getting going. The quarterback situation is in the worst position it has been in under Heupel. Heupel is playing the cards close to his chest and continuing to use gamesmanship by not naming a starter. True freshman Faizon Brandon started the season and after struggling then getting a minor injury, the Vols switched to redshirt freshman George MacIntyre and have not switched back since. MacIntyre has ran the offense better in my opinion, he is less frantic in the pocket and is better at getting the ball out of his hands. The only issue is MacIntyre has not pushed the football down the field much, his 5.7 average depth of target is the lowest in the SEC and is obviously a critical element of Heupel's scheme. MacIntyre will get the start, but I wouldn't be surprised to see a little bit of Faizon Brandon as well to try and throw off Kentucky's defense. Kentucky has faced a dual threat quarterback every week of the season to this point, I am intrigued to see how this pass rush gets after a quarterback that is a pocket passer like MacIntyre. It is something we have yet to see, and this is an area that could be a massive advantage for the Wildcats. It is important that Kentucky wins the early downs on defense and force Tennessee to beat them through the air. Tennessee's offense is led by running back DeSean Bishop, and the Vols will absolutely try to feed him in this football game. Tennessee ranks third in the SEC in yards per rush and EPA per rush, they are very much a run heavy offense. Tennessee is still getting explosive plays in this offense, they have a 12.6 explosive play rate which is third in the conference. The Vols rank second in the SEC with a 15.3 explosive run rate and they rank 13th with a 9.6 explosive pass rate. Tennessee ranks 13th in the SEC in EPA per dropback and yards per pass attempt. They rank 11th in the conference with a 42.5% pass success rate. This is simple for Kentucky, stack the box and slow down this run game. Kentucky has to sell out to stop the run and force the Vols to beat them with their quarterbacks, whether it be MacIntyre or Brandon. DeSean Bishop is one of the best running backs in the country, he has 957 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the season. Bishop is averaging over 100 yards per game and 5.6 yards per carry. He helps the Vols convert on early downs, as their 46.5% early down conversion rate ranks sixth in the SEC. However, they have struggled to convert on third down like Kentucky as they have converted just 35.5% of third down opportunities this season, which ranks 15th in the SEC. In our self scout over the bye week, we pointed out how Kentucky's run defense really improved in the month of October. This has to continue for Kentucky to win this football game, but it will be easier said than done. Jay Bateman has to force Tennessee into a dropback heavy game by getting his defense to stop the run. If they can successfully do that, they will be in a great position to win this game. picks.headline: Tennessee vs Kentucky predictions: Can Vols derail Wildcats’ SEC title hopes?
picks.blurb: November kicks up the stakes in college football, especially with the release of the first College Football Playoff rankings this past Tuesday. And one of Saturday's key games features unlikely SEC contender Kentucky (No. 7 in the US LBM Coaches Poll ) visiting Neyland Stadium to face No. 16 Tennessee . Kentucky landed at No. 6 in the first CFP rankings, while the Vols landed at No. 13, controversially eight spots lower than Alabama — a team it beat by 16 points. Kentucky controls its path to a place it has never been: the SEC championship game. The Wildcats are tied with Georgia atop the conference at 5-1, and winning their final three SEC games would send them to Atlanta. But that run starts with a major obstacle Saturday at Tennessee, where Kentucky has won just 11 times and lost five straight in the rivalry. Florida and Missouri follow, while Georgia faces its own three-game test. First-year Wildcats coach Will Stein isn’t hiding from the stakes, but he knows Kentucky’s historic opportunity disappears quickly if the Wildcats look ahead: “If you don't handle your business this week? Then nothing really matters.” Watch Vols vs Wildcats live on Fubo Tennessee likely needs a 10-2 record to make the playoff. On Saturday, Marcus Freeman could do the same against the same program. No. 11 Notre Dame and No. 1 Miami meet in South Bend with playoff implications on the line in what is the highest-ranked matchup between the programs (according to the AP poll) since that classic Catholics vs. Convicts showdown in 1988. The Irish won the national championship that season, its most recent title. The College Football Playoff selection committee sees a different matchup. Miami sits atop the first CFP rankings, but slotted Notre Dame at No. 11, seven spots lower than the AP voters. Notre Dame is the last team in the CFP field, and a loss against Miami could knock the Irish out of playoff contention entirely. "They don't have that signature win right now," CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek said Tuesday night on ESPN. "They've got a great opportunity in front of them at home versus Miami to get that signature win that I think they need to move up in the rankings." Don't forget, we've been here before. Miami defeated Notre Dame 27-24 in last season's season opener. The Irish remained above Miami in five CFP rankings, but the committee flipped the two in the final week, placing Miami over Notre Dame in the CFP. Miami vs. Notre Dame: Need to know Darian Mensah vs. a defense without its leader : Darian Mensah leads the FBS in completion percentage (80.7%) and pass efficiency (202.7) and is tied for the national lead with 25 touchdown passes against one interception. Notre Dame takes him on without linebacker Drayk Bowen , its leading tackler (45) and the green-dot helmet that relays defensive calls. He was ruled out with an ankle injury suffered against Navy . Malachi Toney's absence : Miami will be without superstar receiver Malachi Toney, who suffered an ankle injury in practice Wednesday and will undergo surgery in hopes of returning for the CFP. This game certainly takes on a different context. The sophomore ranks in the top three nationally in receptions (73), receiving yards per game (128.4) and receiving touchdowns (13), the last of which ties Miami's single-season school record. Cooper Barkate is the second-best receiver on the roster, but he averages 46.5 yards per game, compared to Toney's 128.4. CJ Carr's problem : Carr has been magnificent most of his career, but the splits are wild. He's thrown 18 touchdowns and one interception this season, and he is 15-0 as a starter against unranked teams. Against AP-ranked opponents, he is 2-3, completing 60.9% of his passes at 6.6 yards per attempt with six touchdowns and five interceptions. With few opportunities to impress the CFP committee, he needs to step up against the top-ranked Hurricanes. Unranked Boston College , SMU and Syracuse are the only teams remaining on the schedule. Notre Dame's invincibility : Notre Dame is 10-1 at home against Miami, and the home team has won the last eight on-campus meetings. Miami's only win at Notre Dame Stadium came in 1984. On the other side, the Hurricanes are 18-3 on the road as the AP No. 1, with all three losses at ranked teams, including the 1988 game against the Irish. Miami hasn't defeated an AP top-5 team on the road since 2005. Penalties and the red zone : Notre Dame is the most disciplined team in the FBS, averaging only 28.9 penalty yards per game. Miami ranks 82nd (58.8). The Irish defense, however, ranks 108th in red-zone defense, allowing points on 88.9% of possessions, and Miami scores on 92.9% of its own. History sides with the Irish. Now that Malachi Toney is out, siding with the Irish becomes an easy play. Notre Dame will play the nation's most efficient quarterback either way, but how different does he look without his top option? Meanwhile, Notre Dame's red-zone defense has struggled against far lesser offenses, so will Toney's absence actually matter? Miami is 5-3 against the spread this season. Notre Dame is 4-4. The Irish can win this game, but covering by five points will still be difficult. picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Notre Dame Playoff Problem Ahead of Top-5 Miami Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Notre Dame could find itself in the same College Football Playoff predicament that ended its 2025 season if it can’t beat No. 1 Miami on Saturday, according to ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis. Davis made the case on ESPN’s College GameDay Podcast with co-hosts Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel, saying the No. 4 Fighting Irish (7-1) would be in “ very much the same situation as a year ago ” with a loss. Rece Davis on Notre Dame’s resume Notre Dame Fighting Irish head coach Marcus Freeman reacts during the first half against the Brigham Young Cougars | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis said that split will shape the debate over the Irish. He expects them to stay in the field unless the Hurricanes blow them out, but he doesn’t see the questions about their resume going away. “I think Notre Dame will still be OK absent getting run out of the stadium, which I cannot conceive of happening,” Davis said. “So it’s going to be a little bit different than last year, but the argument, the discussion, is going to be the same if they don’t win this game.” He added: “When you get down to who did you play and who did you beat, especially the who did you beat portion of who did you play, they won’t have much on the paper.” Why does Notre Dame’s schedule matter? General view as Brigham Young Cougars fans celebrate on the field after the game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. The Irish beat Wisconsin, Rice, Michigan State, Purdue, North Carolina, Stanford and Navy. After Miami, they close with Boston College, SMU and Syracuse, who are a combined 14-10 and unranked. Notre Dame does carry a protection it lacked last year. The College Football Playoff guarantees the Irish a spot if they finish in the top 12 of the final rankings. A loss to Miami would test that cushion, though, because Notre Dame would sit at 7-2 with no win over a ranked opponent and no ranked teams left on its schedule. Miami vs. Notre Dame stakes Miami Hurricanes head coach Mario Cristobal celebrates after defeating the Florida State Seminoles | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last season, Miami and Notre Dame both finished 10-2, and the selection committee used the Hurricanes’ 27-24 win in Week 1 to award them the final at-large spot. Last season, Miami and Notre Dame both finished 10-2, and the selection committee used the Hurricanes’ 27-24 win in Week 1 to award them the final at-large spot. The Irish were the first team out and declined a bowl invitation. Notre Dame athletic director Pete Bevacqua said at the time, “ We feel like the playoff was stolen from our student-athletes.” Davis called the rematch “another little delicious subplot” and said Notre Dame’s frustration “wasn’t necessarily just directed at Miami.” Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman made “ leave no doubt ” the program’s mantra for 2026 after the snub. Saturday gives the Irish that chance against an 8-0 Miami team that leads FBS at 47.6 points per game, while Notre Dame’s defense leads FBS at 236.1 yards allowed per game. The committee releases its first College Football Playoff rankings of the season Tuesday at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, and Miami vs. Notre Dame kicks off Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. When it comes to the gambling websites, however, it's a bit different. The odds were released for Saturday's game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in South Bend, Ind. According to Hard Rock Bet, the Hurricanes are a 4.5 underdog in the matchup. This should come as a surprise and it shouldn't. Despite the top ranking, the Hurricanes have shown some flaws this season. Their play on defense has been one of the issues. On Saturday, they gave up 407 yards in the 38-35 victory against the North Carolina Tar Heels. They were assisted by a late fumble recovery and the Tar Heels being twice called for a penalty on two onside kicks to avoid the upset. Despite their dominance on offense, the Hurricanes have given up at least 20 points in three games. They struggled in a 33-20 victory against the Wake Forest Demon Deacons in September. They then needed two overtimes to defeat the Florida State Seminoles in a 45-43 shootout. The Seminoles, who were a failed Hail Mary attempt from stealing a victory, amassed 433 yards. Even though the Hurricanes defeated the Pittsburgh Panthers by 29 points, they still allowed 403 yards. At some point, they need to show they can at least come up with stops should the high-powered offense have an off night. The offense, led by quarterback Darian Mensah, receiver Malachi Toney and running back Mark Fletcher, has carried UM all season. Mensah and Toney are both Heisman candidates while Fletcher just set the school record for most career touchdowns with 38. That is saying a lot considering the amount of talent that has come through Coral Gables over the years. Even though they are favored, the Fighting Irish have struggled the last two games. They had difficulty early on against the Navy Midshipmen before pulling away for a 35-13 victory on Saturday. Two weeks before, Notre Dame was upset by the BYU Cougars of the Big 12 conference. Expect a breakout passing performance, a game-changing takeaway and a decisive finish in one of Week 10's biggest matchups. The College Football Playoff rankings place Georgia second and Ole Miss 10th entering Saturday's showdown. The Bulldogs arrive at 7–1, while the Rebels are 6–2, with kickoff scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. This forecast favors Georgia's offensive balance over the home crowd. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Stockton delivers a career night Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Gunner Stockton will throw for 325 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. That would establish a career high in passing yardage, surpassing the 304 yards listed in Georgia's game notes, and represent an emphatic response to his 101-yard performance against Florida. The prediction hinges on Georgia resisting the temptation to make this exclusively a rushing contest. Early play-action should give Stockton opportunities to attack intermediate windows before Ole Miss settles into its preferred defensive rhythm. The matchup offers a reasonable opening: the Rebels allow 235 passing yards per game, while Stockton has completed 71.8 percent of his attempts this season. Expect Georgia to spread the production rather than funnel everything toward one receiver. Its offensive personnel should allow the Bulldogs to challenge linebackers underneath before testing safeties with deeper routes. The key will be protection discipline. Georgia should prioritize clean pockets over elaborate, slow-developing concepts, letting Stockton build confidence through quick decisions. Once Ole Miss starts anticipating those shorter throws, the Bulldogs can take their shots. The bold part is not simply predicting efficiency. It is forecasting a career-best road performance when Georgia needs its quarterback to create separation rather than merely protect a lead. Georgia scores another defensive touchdown The Bulldogs will intercept Trinidad Chambliss twice and return one takeaway for a touchdown. Ole Miss will also be without running back Kewan Lacy, who was listed out on the initial availability report because of his shoulder injury. That absence could encourage Georgia to devote more attention to containing Chambliss and disrupting his reads. The defensive plan should emphasize controlled pressure. Reckless pursuit would invite escape lanes; disciplined rush angles could force Chambliss to hold the ball or attempt throws into tightening coverage. Expect one interception to come after Georgia initially presents an aggressive front, then drops a defender into an underneath passing lane. The touchdown prediction is ambitious, but Georgia has already scored three defensive touchdowns this season. Another would change the entire complexion of a game in which both offenses should face stretches of frustration. Georgia ends Oxford's winning streak Georgia will win 38–24, ending Ole Miss' 16-game home winning streak. Ole Miss is 3-2 over the last five meetings, but before that, the Bulldogs won ten in a row going back to 1996. How To Watch Georgia vs Ole Miss Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford, MS – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Georgia Will Win The 27-8 win over Florida was Georgia's "enough is enough" moment. After a shaky 27-24 loss to Auburn, hurt by three turnovers, the Bulldogs have two weeks off to rest, and then won the Indoor Cocktail Party by looking deeper, stronger, and far more physical. The running game that didn't get going against Auburn rumbled for 217 yards against the Gators. The Ole Miss defense isn't exactly along for the ride, but … yeah, it sort of is. It's not great overall, but the offense usually makes up for it. However, the team is 0-2 when allowing over 175 rushing yards, and 6-0 when it doesn't. Georgia averages 200 rushing yards per game. The defense was gassed, the team hit a wall, and the Dawgs roared back for a 43-35 win. But the Ole Miss offense worked. In the College Football Playoff, it was a nip-and-tuck game with current head coach Pete Golding's Ole Miss team getting up ten with nine minutes to go. Once again, the defense started to struggle, but this time around, Rebel quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and the offense were able to pull it out in the final moments. And the offense really worked. Yeah, this is a new year, new teams, and the Georgia defense is far more experienced, but Chambliss and the offense are still fantastic. The Rebels still go all out and will make this a track meet. The offense will still work. Georgia vs Ole Miss Prediction, Betting Lines Last year's Georgia team was, in many ways, statistically better than this year's version. However, last year's Bulldog team got roasted by the Ole Miss pace. Georgia allowed 350 yards or more four times last year. Two times were against Ole Miss, once was in a loss to Alabama, and once was a wild overtime win over Tennessee. Georgia allowed over 350 yards just once this season – the 27-24 loss to Auburn. How many times was the Ole Miss offense held to under 400 yards last year? Twice. Once in that first loss to Georgia, the other time in the CFP to Miami. How many times has Ole Miss been held to under 400 yards this year? Once – the loss two weeks ago against Texas. Georgia's defense will do the job this time around when it comes to allowing fewer than 400 yards, and it'll be combined with a ground game that will run 40 times for well over 200 yards. picks.headline: Georgia football coach Kirby Smart previews Ole Miss game
picks.blurb: Georgia football coach Kirby Smart previews Ole Miss game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Georgia football coach Kirby Smart previews Ole Miss game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart heavily praised Ole Miss Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss during his weekly press conference. Smart is quite familiar with Chambliss and Ole Miss . Georgia played Chambliss twice last year including in the Sugar Bowl, which the Rebels won 39-34. Georgia won the regular season meeting in Athens, 43-35. Georgia (7-1, 5-1 SEC) and Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 SEC) are both in the thick of the SEC championship and College Football Playoff hunt. The winner on Saturday night (7:30 p.m. ET on Nov. 7) will find themselves in a much better position while the losers will find themselves much worse off. Specifically, Ole Miss could be facing playoff elimination with a loss to Georgia since the Rebels have an ugly blowout loss to Florida. We're likely looking at another high-stakes shootout between Georgia and Ole Miss. Here's what Georgia coach Kirby Smart said about Ole Miss with most of the media's questions focusing on Chambliss. Smart's opening statement on Ole Miss "It's on to Ole Miss, a really good football team," Smart said at his weekly press conference. "Pete (Golding) has done a tremendous job since taking over. "Obviously, we know the two games last year with them were both really hard-fought battles, hard games, a lot of ebb-and-flow in both games. They've done a tremendous job this year. They probably have the best quarterback in the country who plays at a high level. He is extremely hard to defend and a great player. "I have a lot of respect for their staff. I know a lot of those guys and the team, the way their team competes and plays. They're playing really well right now. At home, they've been exceptionally well. Our guys will be excited for the challenge. Another opportunity. Another week in the SEC, as it always is. It'll be a great atmosphere." On how to defend Chambliss Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) passes the ball against the Louisiana State Tigers "How long do you have?" Smart said. "We could talk for an hour about it, but it's not even that. "I wrote down, so I watched every game, wow plays. It's not the wow plays. The wow plays are what you guys love and what America loves. He had some wow plays against us last year in both games, but especially the second. "It's the down-in, down-out decision making that he's really elite at. The accuracy that he's elite at, the release, the decision. His pinpointing. He has an anticipation of windows that's probably unmatched. I don't know if that was God-given or the fact that he played a lot of football before he got to Ole Miss. He has played a lot of football and experience helps. "You throw all that in, and you have a tremendous athlete. He goes forwards, backwards as fast as he goes sideways. He can back up and go for it. He's just a great athlete that is a great quarterback." On Chambliss' pre-snap and post-snap ability "I can't get inside his head and say what he's doing pre-snap, post-snap," Smart adds. "He's elite at both, in my opinion. He surveys the field. He knows what he's going to do. He's been in this offense long enough that he knows what he's basing his decisions on, and then after the play's snapped, he goes through his progressions and does a great job. "He knows how to navigate a pocket. I think his pocket presence people don't give him enough credit for it. This guy's not just like a take-off-and-run guy. He steps up in the pocket. He goes through the pocket. He's made some of his best 'wow' plays working through the pocket." On Ole Miss' red zone success "You have to play well in the red zone," Smart said. "A lot of that has to do with the quarterback extending plays and running the game. The quarterback run game in the red area really shows up with every team. He's a tremendous decision maker in terms of what he wants to do with the ball. "There's two, three plays in the red area this year that you would say, 'He's never even supposed to pull that ball.' He does it and makes huge plays. He's doing that against SEC teams. That makes him hard to defend in the red area. They got really good skill players, and he's got really good touch and accuracy to make throws. All those things combined to be a good red zone player. "It's hard to say, 'What do you do in the red zone?' You have to play well. You have to play disciplined football, and you have to make it hard to run it in on. That's what most people that are good in the red zone can do." On containing Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense "You have to be successful at a lot of things," Smart notes. "You have to be able to pitch and catch, not just do one thing. There's nothing we're going to do that he hadn't seen. You're not tricking the guy. I think that's what people get infatuated with, is, 'How can I trick him and do that?' You can't do that. "You have to go play good sound football. You have tackle the man that catches it. No yard after catch. You have to create some turnover. You have to bat some balls. You have to make plays and get off the field when you have a chance on third down. There's not a perfect remedy. If there was, somebody would have done it." Follow UGA Wire on Instagram , Facebook , X (formerly Twitter) or Threads for more Georgia football coverage! home.blurb: Georgia (7-1, 5-1 SEC) is No. 2 in the first CFP rankings so it won’t be knocked out of the national title chase with a loss in Saturday night's game in Oxford, Miss., but it could do serious damage to Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2) which is No. 10. “He had some wow plays against us last year,” Georgia coach Kirby Smart said. “Really in both games, but especially the second. But It's the down-in, down-out decision-making that he's really elite at, the accuracy that he's elite at. The release, the decision. He's just pinpoint. He has an anticipation of windows that's probably unmatched.” Georgia: WR Isiah Canion (lower extremity, probable), RB Chauncey Bowens (lower body, questionable), WR Thomas Blackshear (collarbone, questionable), TE Elyiss Williams (undisclosed, questionable), DT Joseph Jonah-Ajonye (undisclosed, questionable), DB Tyriq Green (leg, questionable), LB AJ Kruah (undisclosed, questionable) RB Dante Dowdell (multiple injuries including collarbone, lung and arm, out), OLB Amaris Williams (knee, out). Ole Miss: RB Kewan Lacy (shoulder, out), CB Jalyn Crawford (shoulder, probable), LB Kam Franklin (undisclosed, out), LB Keaton Thomas (undisclosed, out), WR Izaiah Hartrup (undisclosed, out), CB Cedrick Beavers (undisclosed, probable), S Edwin Joseph (undisclosed, out), S MJ Preston (undisclosed, probable), LB Ant Davis (undisclosed, out), WR Kevin Johnson (undisclosed out), S Nascar McCoy (undisclosed, out), S Gerald Lacy (undisclosed, out), OL Carius Curne (undisclosed, out), WR Samari Reed (undisclosed, out), OL Terez Davis (undisclosed, out) Georgia 31, Ole Miss 27: The matchup of Ole Miss's SEC top scoring offense in league games against Georgia's No. 1 scoring defense should be get out your popcorn stuff. Even with Trinidad Chambliss, I trust Georgia to win that battle and get enough plays from Gunner Stockton and the running game to escape Oxford with the victory. Ole Miss DT Will Echoles: The 6-foot-3, 315-pound junior had two tackles for loss, five tackles and two pass breakups in the Sugar Bowl win over Georgia last season. Georgia will need to contain him. Gunner Stockton had several passes batted down against Florida and keeping Echoles out of passing lanes and out of the backfield will be key. He has 21 tackles, 4 tackles for loss and 1 1/2 sacks this season. Ball security will continue to be an issue: Kirby Smart pushed back when asked after the Florida win about another Sacovie-White Helton muff on a punt return, but Georgia has four this season and has fumbled 14 times, which ranks 126th in the nation, according to ESPN's Bill Connelly. Georgia is fortunate to only have lost 5 fumbles this season, but the Bulldogs are living dangerously. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-USA TODAY Sports (Kevin Jairaj, USA TODAY Sports) 1 / 27 PHOTOS: Top highlights from Florida's Cotton Bowl game vs Oklahoma in 2020 PHOTOS: Top highlights from Florida's Cotton Bowl game vs Oklahoma in 2020 'I have a feeling Florida is going to bounce back against Oklahoma' I have a feeling Florida is going to bounce back against Oklahoma, even after last week's disastrous offensive performance against Georgia. The Sooners have been solid defensively this season, but I think Tramell Jones Jr. gets the start and provides the spark the Gators have been missing. I'm expecting a strong first half, with Jadan Baugh playing a major role in establishing the offense. Florida's defense was one of the few bright spots against Georgia, and there's little reason to expect significant regression against an Oklahoma offense that has struggled to score consistently. If the Gators can clean up the turnovers and penalties that have plagued them, I think they can take control early and maintain a comfortable advantage throughout the second half. — David Rosenberg PREDICTION : Florida 28, Oklahoma 14 '(The Gators) will need a big offensive day and to limit turnovers' The Gators need a win to get back on track, and what better way than to face a program in Oklahoma that currently ranks in the SEC's bottom three in points per game. On the other hand, they are one of the conference's better defenses. While their offense has slipped a bit, the Gators have shown progress defensively, and I expect the trend to continue in Ben Hill Griffin. OU has struggled offensively throughout this season, and Florida's defense has been opportunistic in spurts. The Gators have been the better team throughout the season but have had multiple hiccups. To win this game, they will need a big offensive day and to limit turnovers, because this season's numbers show Oklahoma won't be able to keep up. — Michael Trim Jr. PREDICTION: Florida 28, Oklahoma 17 'I think the Gators' defense does enough to stifle Oklahoma' There shouldn't be any panic in Gainesville as the Gators are ahead of schedule in year one of the Jon Sumrall era, but that doesn't mean the early 4-0 start didn't get everyone's hopes up about this ideation of the Gators' roster. Florida showed the country what it was capable of during that first month of the season but reminded the college football world it had a long way to go in order to consistently compete with top programs like Georgia. The key on Saturday is to steady a ship that has been battered with turmoil in the last month. Jadan Baugh and the UF rushing attack have taken a giant step back, several skill position players have been in and out of the lineup and the quarterback now feels extremely uncertain. After Philo's nighmareish first half against Georgia, I anticipate Sumrall will run both he and Tramell Jones Jr. for the OU game. Whoever has the hot hand or creates the most favorable matchup will get the majority of the snaps. Ball security will be the biggest factor for whoever stays on the field, as four turnovers proved costly. Saturday should be a chance for the Gators' defense to shine. picks.headline: Florida Gets Strong Prediction Heading Into Oklahoma Showdown
picks.blurb: Florida Gets Strong Prediction Heading Into Oklahoma Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Florida Gets Strong Prediction Heading Into Oklahoma Showdown (Scott Wachter-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:23 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As the Florida Gators get ready for their upcoming SEC game against the Oklahoma Sooners, the team will have to figure out a way to bounce back. Florida was blown out a week ago by the Georgia Bulldogs, seeing them drop their third game of the season. But the Gators have been a resilient group all year long, and this team will be asked to make it happen again. Entering the game, the Gators hold a record of 5-3 on the year, with the team going 3-3 so far in SEC games. Florida is ranked at No. 23 for the week, staying alive in the first edition of the College Football Playoff rankings. As for the Sooners, they will be coming into the game with a record of 4-4 for the year, going 2-3 in SEC play so far. This team has underperformed this season, but the Gators can't overlook them at all. Oklahoma still has star quarterback John Mateer under center, and he can do damage against this Gators defense. Florida is going to have to be very careful in the game, looking to avoid being upset at home. As the two teams prepare for the SEC battle, the Gators are being favored to come away with the win this week. Florida has been given a 64 percent chance to take down Oklahoma at home, according to the ESPN matchup predictor . One way for the Gators to get an edge in the game is to get running back Jadan Baugh back into a strong rhythm. After an incredible start to the season, the star back has slowed down heavily, with him going 100 yards on the ground for four straight games. Baugh still has put together a special season for Florida, with him rushing for 801 yards with 13 touchdowns. But when the Gators are at their best, Baugh is going up and down the field, opening the offense up. If Florida is able to get Baugh going again this week, it could help the offense out, giving the team a much stronger chance to take down the Sooners. Oklahoma can have an explosive offensive attack, so the Gators may be forced to put up points in order to keep up with them. Kickoff for this game between the Gators and the Sooners is scheduled for 4:45 p.m. PT/7:45 p.m. ET from Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Gainesville.

picks.blurb: Florida Given Favorable Odds to Defeat Oklahoma in Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Florida Given Favorable Odds to Defeat Oklahoma in Week 10 (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Mon, November 2, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Not only did the spread for the Florida Gators vs. Oklahoma Sooners open at four-points, but it later moved two-points further in the Gators favor. Head coach Jon Sumrall let his thoughts be heard after a brutal loss in Atlanta, but at the end of the day there's no shame in losing to the now No. 2-ranked Georgia Bulldogs. Still, dropping a third game this year stung quite a bit, and Florida had far too many things work against them in that game. Most of their wounds were self inflicted, so that's a major focal point heading into Week 10 when Oklahoma comes to town. The Sooners are just 2-3 in conference play, and they're now six-point underdogs, according to DraftKings , ahead of this matchup on Saturday, Nov. 7. At the time of writing, the money line is set at -205 for Florida, meaning a $205 bet would win $100 in return. No one is anticipating that this game will be a blowout, nor should they be as Florida has a bad home loss this year to South Carolina. That Ole Miss win was quickly forgotten about after the Gators were embarrassed on the road at Missouri, and then back at home against the Gamecocks. Remember, this is the same Oklahoma team that beat Texas a few weeks ago, so while it's an impressive feat for Florida to have, the Sooners are in the same conversation. Oklahoma is +170 in the money line, so a $100 bet would net $170 should the Sooners prevail. The over-under is currently set at 47.5 points, though that seems low with how these defenses have played this season. As always, the spread, over-under, and money line will fluctuate throughout the week, though it was quite notable to see Florida jump to six-point favorites after it only opened as a four-point spread. To say there's a quarterback controversy in Gainesville would be an understatement. Aaron Philo looked horrendous in Atlanta, so it's safe to assume that Tramell Jones Jr. will be the Week 10 starter. Oklahoma has John Mateer leading the way, and he's meant everything to a Sooners team that has just 854 rushing yards as a team. For reference, Jadan Baugh has 801 himself, so that's one of the clear areas where the Gators should have an advantage, at least on paper, going into this one.

picks.headline: Florida vs. Oklahoma Final Score Predictions: Experts predict fascinating battle between two traditional powers with QB issues
picks.blurb: Florida vs. Oklahoma Final Score Predictions: Experts predict fascinating battle between two traditional powers with QB issues - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Scott Wachter-Imagn Images, BRYAN TERRY/THE OKLAHOMAN-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness · AtoZ Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Florida Gators and Oklahoma Sooners meet for the first time in SEC play, and both teams have questions at quarterback. The Florida Gators and Oklahoma Sooners are set to meet for just the third time in history on Saturday night, and it will be the first game in The Swamp. In the history of both programs, they have met twice: 2008 BCS National Championship Game (Florida won 24- 14) and 2020 Cotton Bowl (Oklahoma won 55-20). This year, it will be a much different game than both before it, as both quarterback spots are in a tough spot. The Gators have a quarterback controversy with Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr., while Oklahoma has had numerous issues with John Mateer, leading to the dismissal of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle. Who will get the win and take one step forward? It's primed to be a great game, and our experts predicted the game. Florida 20, Oklahoma 9 It was disappointing to see the Gators fail to take advantage of their impressive defensive performance against the Georgia Bulldogs, but it was two consecutive plus performances for a unit that has been rough this season. Now you give that unit John Mateer with Jason Witten calling plays for the first time? This could be a disaster for the Sooners. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Florida 34, Oklahoma 13 Florida likely saw their playoff hopes extinguished last weekend against Georgia, but they've got a golden opportunity to get right on Saturday at home against Oklahoma. The Sooners fired offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle after a blowout home loss to South Carolina, and there's no reason to believe that things are going to improve on the road against a Gators defense that held Georgia relatively in check offensively last week. Jadan Baugh and the Gators get things rolling early, and Oklahoma lacks the horses to keep this a game by mid-third quarter. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Florida 21, Oklahoma 10 This game is going to be a grind, with neither offense finding much consistency throughout the afternoon. Oklahoma's defense will do its part to keep the Sooners in it, making life difficult for the Gators and keeping the score within one possession for much of the game. But John Mateer and the Oklahoma offense continue to look like a major problem. The Sooners struggle to sustain drives, miss opportunities and put too much pressure on their defense to carry the load. Florida won't exactly light up the scoreboard either, but the Gators will do enough to eventually pull away. Their defense should take advantage of Oklahoma's offensive struggles, while the offense finds just enough success to put points on the board. The game stays uncomfortably close into the fourth quarter before Florida puts together a late scoring drive to finally seal it. It won't be pretty, but the Gators will take it. Florida wins 21-10. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Florida 27, Oklahoma 20 This game features two teams on opposite ends of the preseason spectrum. Yes, the Gators have 3 losses heading into November, but they have some of the best wins in the conference after beating Ole Miss and Texas. The Gators look to be in good hands with Jon Sumrall for years to come, as he has exceeded all year-one expectations. For OU, things couldn't have gone more wrong. John Mateer regressed, the offense has been horrific, and OC Ben Arbuckle was just let go this week. Still, the defense and Brent Venables will create trouble for a Florida Gators offense that can look like one of the best in the country one week, and a mess the next. But catching the Sooners in the swamp will be a win for Florida. I expect Jadan Baugh and the defense to do enough to prevent the new OC bump for the Sooners. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Florida 23, Oklahoma 17 Florida is coming off a blowout loss to Georgia that'll have them wanting to get right at home. Oklahoma making staff changes could result in some early juice from the Sooners' offense, as we sometimes see with programs after a big change. However, I think the Gators are going to move to 6-3 and keep alive what has been a solid first season for Jon Sumrall in Gainesville. The QB situation is going to matter against a talented Oklahoma defense, but the Gators will figure it out. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Oklahoma To nobody's surprise, our experts are in favor of the Gators here. The Sooners are in a really tough spot, and a trip to The Swamp with a first-time play caller isn't likely to help any. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. home.headline: Florida has 7 players on initial SEC Availability Report for Week 10
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Four Gators are listed as out: defensive lineman Jeramiah McCloud, tight end Evan Chieca, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji and linebacker Jaden Robinson. McCloud is out due to a suspension, according to Swamp247 , while Robinson missed his first game of the season last week against Georgia. Listed as doubtful is wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed the last four games with a grade-1 PCL strain that he suffered against Ole Miss in Week 4 that was re-aggravated ahead of last week's Georgia game. "So he was not available at practice today," Jon Sumrall said on Monday . "I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." The two players listed as questionable are wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. Stockton has been dealing with a nagging foot injury but still played against the Bulldogs last week, finishing with 76 yards on eight catches. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas and offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis are listed as doubtful, while wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, defensive backs Peyton Bowen and Eli Bowen, tight end Rocky Beers and defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu are listed as questionable, and offensive lineman Jake Maikkula is listed as probable. WR Bailey Stockton — questionable DL Emmanuel Oyebadejo — questionable OL Eddy Pierre-Louis — doubtful WR Jer'Michael Carter — questionable DL Kenny Ozowalu — questionable OL #69 Jake Maikkula — probable Questionable (50% chance to play) The initial SEC availability report for college football's Week 10 was released on Wednesday night; the Florida Gators have seven players listed, while the Oklahoma Sooners have a whopping 16. "Jeramiah McCloud has been suspended for this week's game against Oklahoma for conduct detrimental to the team. His status with the program will be re-evaluated after this week's contest," per a statement from a program spokesperson. Sumrall added what he called his "official VB3 statement": "He wants to play. He's doing everything he can to play. He's pissed off he can't play, and he's doing everything in his power to play. It's a real injury that we thought we were on the other side of that he had a setback last week, and it sucks. I mean, it freaking sucks for him." Oklahoma has eight players who are not expected to play on Saturday: linebacker Taylor Heim, defensive back Dakoda Fields, wide receiver Trell Harris, linebacker Cole Sullivan, tight end Trynae Washington, defensive back Jacobe Johnson, and offensive linemen Ryan Fodje and Fred Hinton.
